result.summary:
Study result for the 3D renderer ("RoadRenderer3D") of the Modern mode. Repo untouched (git status clean); all work in the scratch dir, 7.6 MB of evidence kept.

1) WORLD MODEL – measured, not guessed. I dumped curve/height of all 128 real stage directions (3,018 km of visible road) and integrated the true heading. Result: a true world-space 3D track is viable. Within everything that can be loaded at once (road parts 360–1,900 m apart by path) the closest two parts ever come is 267.6 m – and that is just the chord of the tightest bends, not a loop. Globally the road is NOT consistent: in 8 stage directions the integrated centreline crosses itself (3.9–11 m), but always with 2,544–6,576 m of path in between, i.e. never inside one loaded window. Consequence: true 3D works if chunks are streamed strictly by path distance and nothing is stored world-fixed beyond the window. I also showed that Arcade's projection is mathematically a static SHEARED world (X(s)=double integral of curvature) seen through a shear view matrix – that is the exact-parity alternative (b); I recommend against it as default (per-frame shear of every chunk, rigid objects need special shaders, the road still "slides sideways"), but keep it as a fallback behind one RoadPath class.

2) SPIKE – a 600-line prototype behind the existing renderer interface (setup/render/perf_stats, started with --gfx=modern) driven by the real RaceSession, autopilot and traffic: true-arc road chunks from the real Track, chase camera, sun with shadows, depth fog from view.visibility_m, boxes as vehicles, the existing prop sprites as billboards, signs drawn by the existing SignPainter into SubViewport textures, the existing RaceBackdrop as 3D background (Environment.BG_CANVAS). All of it runs on Godot 4.7.2 Compatibility (llvmpipe). On a straight the 3D camera reproduces Arcade's projection to 0.0 px (10–600 m). Measured: chunk (96 m) mesh 1.0 ms avg / 2.6 ms max in GDScript + 0.15 ms props; renderer GDScript per frame 0.26–1.14 ms (1–23 cars) against 5.36 ms for Arcade's _draw on the same machine; spike scene 43–97 draw calls and 10–16k triangles in the visible pass. GPU time on a Steam Deck is NOT measured (no GPU here) – only inferred from these proxies.

3) FAIRNESS – proven with numbers for the practical criterion (stopping sight distance), not for the literal one. Crests: same camera position and same heights (Track.y, hill scale 2.0 baked in) give identical sight lines on straights; over 5,923 targets in all stages 3D sees a car later by more than 6 m in 76 cases (1.28 %), earlier in 41, and in 0 cases later AND inside the stopping sight distance. Curves: with a tangent camera true 3D loses the far end of tight bends earlier than Arcade (first differences at 200 m); with a look-into-the-curve yaw (0.6 x bearing of the road 100 m ahead) there is no case up to 270 m in 86.6 million samples, and beyond that every case is at least 1.7x farther away than the stopping sight distance at the fastest drivable speed (dry, rain, snow).

4) MAIN NEW WORK AND RISK: terrain and horizon closure. Arcade paints every ground row across the full screen; true 3D needs a terrain surface. The spike shows the problem (pale void beyond a 100 m ribbon) and a first remedy (rings to 480 m). Measured limits: a ruled ribbon of 120 m half width never conflicts inside the loaded window, 480 m is free on 97.35 % of the road sides (the rest is the inside of bends). This is its own module with its own fairness rule and test.

Deliverables below: full inventory of what Arcade shows and how each element maps to 3D, world-model decisions, engineering (nodes, chunks, shaders, instancing, vehicles, lights, shadows, signs, sky, weather, post, presets, interface, switching, fallback, Deck budget), a module breakdown for parallel implementation with a first vertical slice, and the test strategy.
result.recommendation:
Build Modern as a true world-space 3D renderer (lead's hypothesis confirmed, with three conditions). (1) World: heading integrated per 3 m segment (exact arcs, midpoint rule), cross-sections perpendicular to the tangent, heights = Track.y unchanged, chunks of 32 segments (96 m) with chunk-local vertices and a floating origin, streamed by PATH distance (load when path distance <= 1,500 m and distance by air <= visibility + 96 m; landmarks to 1,900 m), nothing world-persistent. All positions go through one class RoadPath3D.world(z, x, h), so the sheared Arcade-parity mapping stays available as a fallback without touching the builders. (2) Camera: exactly Arcade's projection as the base (Camera3D frustum, focal 711 px at 1280, horizon at 45 % via frustum_offset, same position 9 m behind / 3.4 m above the road at the car, no pitch) plus a look-into-the-curve yaw (0.6 x bearing 100 m ahead, max 12.6 degrees); every further camera effect may only widen what is seen. (3) Fairness as tests, not as intent: static scenery fogs by distance (never more than Arcade), vehicles and signs additionally fade by path distance exactly like Arcade's item alpha, terrain never rises above the road inside the sight corridor of bends, indicators keep Arcade's minimum pixel size; three headless checks (frustum, crest/terrain line of sight, path clearance >= 250 m within 1,900 m) run over all stages in tools/run_tests.sh.

Reuse instead of rebuild for v0.8.0: RaceBackdrop as background canvas, SignPainter as texture source, existing sprites as far-LOD billboards (0 extra bytes), Palette as the single source for sun/ambient/fog. Keep GDScript per frame under 1.5 ms by making everything static per chunk; street, tunnel and canopy lamps are emissive meshes plus analytical light pools in the road shader, real lights are limited to sun (2 shadow splits on the Deck), 1–2 player spots and a pool of 6 omni lights.

Start with a vertical slice that productionises the spike (interface + RoadPath3D + camera + road chunks + ribbon terrain + billboard props + sign atlas + box/first-mesh vehicles + sun/fog/backdrop + the three fairness tests), then run terrain, structures (tunnel, bridges/water, fuel/border/city), props/landmarks, vehicles, lighting/weather and the asset export in parallel against the ChunkBuilder interface. Decide early whether the user can test a build on a real Steam Deck: the GPU budget is the one thing this machine cannot measure.
decisions: WORLD MODEL – choose (a) true world-space 3D. Evidence (all 128 stage directions, 3,018 km road): nearest other road part within 360–1,900 m of path is 267.6 m (bukarest_sibiu from Sibiu; all ten worst cases are chords of single tight bends at exactly the 360 m lower bound), so nothing loaded together ever overlaps. Max heading change inside 900 m: median 60 deg, p90 101 deg, max 219 deg; road ahead turned more than 90 deg at 0.78 % of camera positions (a far road across the bend, visible in 3D, off screen in Arcade). Curviness 3 (R >= 134 m) is only 494 of 29,400 odometer km (1.7 %), curviness 2 10.6 %.

WORLD MODEL – the 3D world is only locally consistent: 8 of 128 stage directions cross themselves in true 3D (3.9 m Erfurt–Kassel, 4.1 m Sibiu–Timisoara, 4.7/4.8 m San Sebastian–Burgos both ways, 8.7 m Bordeaux–San Sebastian, 9.2/10.4 m Saragossa–Pau both ways, 11.0 m Bukarest–Sibiu), always with 2,544–6,576 m of path between the two passes. Handling: stream by path distance only, every piece of world (terrain, props, lights) is owned by its chunk and freed with it, no world-space caches, no world-grid terrain. A world-grid heightfield terrain was considered and rejected for exactly this reason.

WORLD MODEL – guard for future stages: headless validator in tools/run_tests.sh (min distance by air >= 250 m for parts 360–1,900 m apart by path; loops only beyond 2,000 m). A new stage that fails gets another seed (data fix, no records to protect). Runtime guard as defence only: terrain width is clamped by a per-row clearance table.

WORLD MODEL – (b) sheared 'bent world' rejected as default but documented as fallback. Insight: Arcade's projection equals a static world with centreline (X(s), Y(s), s), X = double integral of curvature, viewed with a shear instead of a rotation; so (b) needs no vertex-shader bending, only one shear transform per chunk per frame, and gives pixel parity and no self-intersection ever. Against it: every chunk transform changes every frame in curves, rigid objects (props, buildings, lights) must be re-orthonormalised in a custom vertex shader or updated on the CPU, lights/particles live in sheared space, and the picture keeps the pseudo-3D feel (road slides sideways, world never turns). Kept available because all builders address positions only through RoadPath3D.

WORLD MODEL – (c) hybrids rejected: camera-relative bending with a lookup table in the vertex shader (saturating relative heading) needs bend code in every material including imported glTF materials, breaks engine culling and shadow-frustum fitting, and swims like Arcade; chunk-rigid chains with compressed joints crack at chunk borders.

CROSS-SECTION FRAME – perpendicular to the tangent (heading at the segment boundary), vehicles placed at P(z) + x*N(z). Screen-parallel sections only exist in the sheared model. Cost in parity: lateral points 11 m ahead deviate up to 4.9 px in a slight curve and 22 px in the tightest bend (measured). Sim semantics unchanged (x is lateral in road coordinates); a 16.5 m truck on the inside lane of the tightest bend is 3 % longer than its lane arc (0.46 m) – negligible.

ARCS – exact arcs, integrated per 3 m segment with the midpoint rule (theta += curve/R1 * L; P += L * f(theta_mid)); polyline error inside a segment is 8 mm at R = 134 m. Parabola (Arcade) and arc agree to 0.0 px on straights, <= 6 px up to 150 m at R = 400 m, 7–19 px at 200–600 m; at R = 136 m 11–22 px up to 100 m, 53 px at 150 m, 122 px at 200 m (objects are also up to 24 % larger there because depth by air is shorter than by road).

HILL HEIGHTS – use Track.y as it is (render.hill_height_scale 2.0 is already baked into the segment heights; physics uses grade/hill_scale). Same heights + same camera position = identical crest sight lines, and the crest warning signs (computed on these heights) stay meaningful. No separate scale for Modern. Optional later: visual superelevation in curves (no effect on sight).

CAMERA BASE – Camera3D.set_frustum(size = near*720/711, offset.y = size*(0.45-0.5), near 0.3–0.5, far 2,600): reproduces RoadProjection exactly (0.0 px on a straight from 10 to 600 m, measured with unproject_position). Position = Arcade's (camera_z, camera_x, camera_y from the view), no pitch, horizon fixed. Shake = frustum-offset jitter in pixels as in Arcade. The session's render interpolation is used as is.

CAMERA MODERN ADDITIONS – look-into-the-curve yaw = 0.6 x bearing of the centreline 100 m ahead (function of position only, so deterministic for tests and replays): max 12.6 deg, player car off-centre p99 57 px, max 135 px. Milder alternative 0.5 x at 60 m: max 6.4 deg / 56 px (on-screen parity to 200 m, 282 of 710,280 cases at 250 m; stopping-distance check not run for it). Further effects only if they never reduce the view: FOV kick (wider only), camera may move back but never closer or lower, roll <= 1.5 deg. Offer 'Kamera: klassisch' (gain 0) as an option.

DRAW DISTANCE AND FOG – two laws. Static scenery: engine depth fog (Environment.FOG_MODE_DEPTH works in Compatibility), begin = 0.45 x visibility, end slightly beyond visibility, curve calibrated by a render check so contrast at every depth is >= Arcade's (Arcade: ground mixes linearly to fog, item alpha = 1 - t^2). Dynamic items (vehicles, signs): additionally fade by PATH distance with Arcade's _item_alpha in their shader (dither), so nothing pops in on a far road and visibility equals the model the simulation and tests/sim/sight_check.gd assume (seen = 0.839 x visibility). Landmarks keep their own law (landmark_fade: 2 x visibility, max 1,900 m) in a shader with engine fog disabled.

CHUNK LOADING RANGE – load a chunk when path distance <= 1,500 m AND distance by air <= visibility + 96 m. Reason: the road point 900 m ahead by path is nearer than 800 m by air at 1.06 % of camera positions (min 411 m), so loading by path <= 900 m alone would pop in unfogged; points 1,500 m ahead by path are within 900 m by air at 0.38 %. The renderer forces Track generation that far ahead (get_segment; deterministic, sequential) and builds the sign layer of a chunk only once its segments are final (generation frontier minus generation_lead_m, 600 m).

FAIRNESS, CURVES (frustum) – measured over all stages, camera every 6–12 m, targets 50–755 m, three lanes. Tangent camera: Arcade on screen but 3D not in 0 cases to 150 m, 35 at 200 m, 564 at 250 m (of 710,280 each). Yaw 0.6@100 m: 0 cases up to 270 m (86.6 M samples), then 13 at 280 m rising to ~2,300 at 650 m; in every one of them the stopping sight distance at the fastest drivable speed (best lateral grip, braking envelope, 1 s reaction) is at most 0.59 x the distance (dry 0.58, rain 0.59, snow 0.55). Literal 'at least as early everywhere' is not achievable in true 3D; 'early enough to stop, with 1.7x margin' is.

FAIRNESS, CRESTS – 5,923 targets (every 300 m where the road is not flat), car body 0.75 m and sign board 2.8 m, terrain modelled as a ribbon at road height (half width min(100 m, 0.8 R)): cars seen later in 3D by > 6 m in 76 cases (1.28 %), by > 30 m in 22, earlier in 41; signs 72 later / 40 earlier. Later AND inside the stopping sight distance: 0 (cars) and 0 (signs). Arcade itself shows 13.78 % of targets from less than the stopping sight distance (the blind crests the warning signs exist for); 3D 13.74 %. The large differences (e.g. 750 m vs 186 m) are real geometry: in true 3D one cannot look through the hill a road winds around.

FAIRNESS RULES FOR ART – (1) terrain relief is never above the road level of its cross-section inside the sight corridor: inside of a bend up to the sagitta of a 300 m chord (d^2/8R: 84 m at R = 134 m, 28 m at R = 400 m), elsewhere up to 8 m from the paved edge; negative relief is free. (2) Extra decorative vegetation never on the inside of bends within that corridor. (3) Indicators keep Arcade's minimum screen size (2.4 x 2 px lamp, 4.5 px glow) through a flare billboard. (4) Night ambient and tail-light emission are calibrated so a tail light at 0.839 x visibility is above a pixel-luminance threshold. (5) No depth of field, no darkening vignette over the road.

TERRAIN – ruled ribbon owned by the chunk: rings at 0/5/15/40/100/220/480 m beyond the shoulder with heights from the road height of the same cross-section plus relief (TerrainProfile.height(s, side, lateral), a pure function used by the mesh builder, by prop placement and by the fairness test). Measured free width inside the loaded window: 120 m on 100 % of road sides, 160 m 99.92 %, 240 m 99.66 %, 320 m 99.29 %, 480 m 97.35 %; the limit is the inside of bends (clamp to 0.8 R) and is read from a per-row clearance table. Beyond the ribbon: a far-ground plane following the camera at the smoothed road height, coloured like distant ground, fogged by distance; the backdrop stands on the horizon row. Spike evidence shows both the problem (100 m ribbon: pale void) and that wide rings close most of it; a gap remains on the outside of climbing bends (pair_sp172_1) – this is the module with the highest visual risk.

STREAMING AND PRECISION – chunk = 32 segments (96 m), about 11 live at 900 m visibility, vertices relative to the chunk origin, chunk nodes relative to a floating origin that is re-based when the camera is more than ~2 km away (max coordinate of the true path is 37.8 km = 4 mm float precision without it). World yaw 0 = heading at the session start, so the camera yaw equals view.bg_offset up to the look yaw and the sun in the backdrop matches the shadow direction.

CHUNK BUILDING – three phases per builder: collect (main thread, snapshot of the 33 TrackSegments and their sprites, ~0.1–0.2 ms), build (pure arrays, WorkerThreadPool), commit (main thread: ArrayMesh/MultiMesh + add_child, at most one chunk per frame, all visible chunks at load). Measured in the spike on the main thread: mesh 0.97–1.09 ms avg, p95 1.2–1.5, max 1.9–2.6 ms for 520–690 quads; billboard props 0.14–0.18 ms; first frame with 11–13 chunks 13–23 ms. Estimate for the full builders: 3–5x, hence threaded. At 250 km/h 0.72 chunks per second are needed. Note: Track generation itself (existing, already paid by Arcade in the sim step) costs 0.9–2.0 ms per 96 m with peaks of 6–10 ms.

MATERIALS AND SHADERS – road.gdshader: asphalt colour per road type, lane/edge/dash lines, checker and crosswalk computed from UV + per-vertex lane data (no overlay geometry, no z-fighting; the spike used coplanar strips instead), wetness/snow/night as global uniforms, analytical light pools (player cone, <= 6 traffic cones, <= 16 lamp pools – the formulas of RoadRenderer._light), retro-reflective term for markings. terrain.gdshader: two scenery colours + noise, snow by normal, same light pools. water.gdshader: animated normals, Fresnel to the palette sky colour, sun glints, night city lights. tunnel: unlit-ish interior with lamp emission and tunnel palette. vehicle.gdshader: paint colour, light slots (tail, brake, indicator L/R, beacon phase) and fade as instance uniforms. prop.gdshader: wind sway, snow, night window emission. Engine quirks found: directional light energy acts about pi times stronger than albedo x energy (sun 0.2 + ambient 0.5 matched Arcade's daylight colours within ~10 %), and two-sided materials flip normals of back faces, so winding must be consistent (cull back in production).

INSTANCING AND LOD FOR PROPS – one MultiMeshInstance3D per mesh and chunk (expected 76 props per 900 m on the median scenery, 155 on the densest). LOD0/LOD1 meshes near, the EXISTING sprite sheets as Y-billboards far (alpha scissor, verified in the spike with trees, rocks, cliffs: 0 extra bytes, also the stand-in for any prop whose mesh does not exist yet). Mirrored-left and edge-aligned placement, tint and fallback rules come from the same prop dictionaries Arcade uses. Compatibility has no cross-fade for visibility ranges (to be confirmed by the engine probe): switch at distances where fog and size hide the pop.

VEHICLES – pool of instances keyed by the view's vehicle id (player -1, police -2). Transform from two path points (rear and front of the collision box), so yaw and pitch follow the road and the footprint is exactly the collision box; own heading from lateral speed (renderer measures x per id as Arcade does), player adds steer x 3 deg, understeer x 6 deg, roll from lateral acceleration, blinking via the view's visible flag. Lights are emissive material slots driven per instance (tail = night/tunnel, brake, blink with the 0.72 s period, beacon a/b). Trucks and buses become real meshes (cab + trailer). LOD0 near, LOD1, LOD2 box beyond ~150 m. Measured cost of the naive spike: about 38 microseconds per car and frame.

LIGHT BUDGET – real lights: 1 directional (sun/moon) with shadows, 1–2 SpotLight3D for the player's headlights (verified), a pool of 6 OmniLight3D moved each frame to the nearest street/tunnel/canopy lamps or the police beacon so vehicles and props are lit there. Everything else is emissive geometry plus the analytical pools in the road/terrain shaders: a tunnel has a lamp every 12 m (75 in view), a city a street light every 33 m – far beyond the Compatibility limits (8 lights per object, 32 renderable by default). Glow replaces Arcade's additive halos; occlusion comes from the depth buffer, so the whole glow-occlusion machinery (crest line, bands, tunnel window, vehicle hulls) is not needed in 3D.

SHADOWS – directional only. Deck/Mittel: 2 PSSM splits, 2048 px, 120 m; Hoch: 4 splits, 4096 px, 200 m; Niedrig: none, blob shadows under vehicles. Casters: vehicles, buildings, structures, tree shadow proxies (opaque blobs instead of alpha-tested crowns); terrain and road only receive; signs and billboards do not cast. In the spike 2 splits added 8.7k–19k shadow primitives.

SIGNS – SignAtlas: every distinct sign (kind|text|value|country|road|wall|limit) is drawn once by the existing SignPainter into a SubViewport and used as texture on a quad in the cross-section plane with real posts (verified: chevrons, crest and limit signs in the spike). Pre-render all textures of a stage at load from Track's event list (creating them on demand cost up to 10.5 ms in a chunk build), convert to mipmapped ImageTextures, tolerate headless (no readback). Gantries (start with countdown lamps, finish with ZIEL banner), fuel price pylon, canopy and border fascia use the same painter for their lettering on mesh panels. Retro-reflection = emission that rises with night and headlight distance.

SKY, BACKDROP, SKYLINE, LANDMARK SILHOUETTES – v0.8.0 reuses RaceBackdrop unchanged on a CanvasLayer below the 3D scene (Environment.BG_CANVAS with background_canvas_max_layer; verified in Compatibility): gradient sky, sun/moon/stars, clouds, all nine silhouette styles, skyline with lit windows, landmark silhouettes, style blending. Heading = camera yaw, base line = horizon row (computed from the far ground inside the frustum; using all path points was wrong in true 3D). Ambient light comes from Palette (AMBIENT_SOURCE_COLOR). Upgrade path inside Modern: replace draw_sky by a sky shader (clouds, sun disc) while keeping the silhouettes.

WEATHER AND PARTICLES – Palette stays the single source: sun direction/colour/energy, ambient, fog colour and range, global shader uniforms (wetness, snow, night). Rain and snow as GPUParticles3D in camera space (CPUParticles3D fallback), spray emitters pooled for the nearest vehicles, wet road = darker + smoother + analytical tail-light streaks (or additive mirror quads under near vehicles, as Arcade does), snow whitening by surface normal plus snow banks at the road edge, tunnel: no weather, own ambient/fog, exposure ramp at the exit instead of Arcade's over-exposed outside palette.

POST-PROCESSING AND QUALITY PRESETS – Compatibility offers glow, tonemap, adjustments, MSAA, 3D render scale; no SSR, SSAO, volumetrics (engine probe to confirm details). Presets: Niedrig (no shadows, no MSAA, no glow, far LOD from 80 m, 60 % vegetation, render scale 0.85), Mittel = Steam Deck default (2 splits/2048/120 m, MSAA 2x, glow, LOD0 to 60 m, billboards from 200 m, 4 pooled lights), Hoch (4 splits/4096/200 m, MSAA 4x, LOD0 to 120 m, billboards from 350 m, 130 % vegetation, 8 pooled lights), Auto (2 s start benchmark + adapter name). MSAA and render scale are set on the viewport at setup and restored on exit.

COMMON RENDERER INTERFACE – duck-typed contract for both renderers, created by one factory: setup(track, proj, cfg, scenery_db), render(view), perf_stats(), plus new mode(), preload_assets(sets), set_quality(preset), world_to_screen(z, x, h), healthy(). The spike needed exactly three edits in race_session.gd (type of the renderer variable, factory branch, typed perf dictionary). The view dictionary needs no new mandatory key; Arcade is not touched, so it stays pixel-identical (guarded by golden-frame hashes). Tests that read Arcade internals (check_glow_occlusion, shoot_vehicles, bench_render, check_session 'preload') set gfx = arcade explicitly.

MODE SELECTION, SWITCHING, FALLBACK – Settings.graphics_mode ('arcade'|'modern') and graphics_quality, options entry 'Grafik: Arcade / Modern', CLI --gfx=arcade|modern and --gfx-quality=, setup key gfx for tests/attract. Switching = free one renderer node and create the other (renderers hold no simulation state); allowed in the options and, if wanted, in the pause menu. Fallback to Arcade with a visible message when: the model manifest is missing or broken, a start self-test (tiny SubViewport scene with the key shaders, read back) fails, the adapter is a software renderer, or a watchdog sees the frame time above budget at the lowest preset; quality steps down first.

STEAM DECK BUDGET (1280x720 inside 1280x800, 60 fps) – GDScript main thread: renderer <= 1.5 ms on a PC core (spike 0.26–1.14 ms), so Modern frees 4–5 ms compared with Arcade's _draw (5.36 ms measured here); chunk commits <= 2 ms per frame. GPU proxies as limits for bench_modern: <= 250 draw calls visible + <= 100 shadow, <= 300k triangles per frame including shadows (planned split: vehicles ~75k, props ~60k, road/terrain ~20k, structures ~15k, shadow passes rest), 1 shadowed light with 2 splits, <= 8 unshadowed real lights, alpha-scissor foliage only, particles <= 500. Measured here: GDScript ms, draw calls, triangles. Inferred: that this fits the Deck GPU.

INVENTORY A, road and ground (RoadRenderer._draw_ground/_draw_markings) -> 3D. Road types autobahn (3 lanes, guardrails, paved right shoulder 2.5 m, left 0.8 m paved + grass median), landstrasse (2 lanes, gravel/grass verge), city (2 lanes, curbs 0.14 m, sidewalks, no edge lines); fractional lane transitions over 180 m; fuel lane with 40 m tapers, hatched wedge, wide separator, extra edge line; asphalt shade per type with alternating 6 m bands; edge lines 0.3 m, lane lines 0.15 m dashed 6/12 m (city 3/6 m), dropped beyond 260 m; checkered start (z = 14 m) and finish lines; crosswalks every 330 m; grass in two-tone 12 m bands per scenery with outskirts-to-centre blend over 150 m; wet darkening with sky sheen; snow ground, snow strips at the road edge; tunnel walkways. -> road/shoulder/curb/sidewalk strips from RoadMeshBuilder, all paint in road.gdshader, ribbon terrain with terrain.gdshader, weather through global uniforms.

INVENTORY B, structures (_draw_structures and helpers) -> 3D. Guardrails (three bands 0.48–0.8 m, posts every 6 m, reflectors every 50 m amber right / white left) -> extruded profile + post MultiMesh + emissive reflectors. Delineators every 50 m -> MultiMesh. Tunnel (tiled walls to 2.9 m, concrete to 4.2 m, haunches, ceiling 6.2 m, two lamp rows every 12 m, green emergency niches every 150 m, walkways, darkness fog 260 m, 45 m peek from outside, portal hill with headwall, wing walls, frame, conifers; wall-mounted signs; over-exposed exit) -> tube mesh, emissive lamps + shader pools + pooled omnis, portal mound mesh closing the terrain, tunnel environment blend. Fuel station (islands with yellow curb, canopies with light panels and fascia lettering, pillars, pumps, shop, price pylon) -> procedural canopy/island meshes per zone + glTF pump/shop + painter textures. Border (roof 6 m with pillars, fascia with EU emblem and local name incl. Cyrillic, lights, customs booths both sides) -> procedural roof + glTF booths. City (street lights every 33 m alternating with light pools, fences picket/hedge/wall/iron with gaps, buildings both sides mirrored left, street trees) -> meshes + MultiMesh. Bridges (water at water level with quay walls/embankments, sky reflection, glints, night shimmer; railings steel/balustrade/iron/parapet; truss girders 4.2 m and portals every 40 m; cable-stayed pylons with cable fans and warning lights; bridge lamps every 24/36 m; houseboats and ships; deck 0.4 m wider outside the city) -> deck strips, water.gdshader plane, extruded railings/girders, pylon + cable meshes, boat props.

INVENTORY C, items -> 3D. Scenery props: 86 sprite sets, rules of 22 landscapes + 40 city landscapes (17 building styles), e.g. north_plain: bush_round, farmhouse, haybale, tree_birch, tree_oak, wind_turbine; forest_hills: rock_a, tree_beech, tree_pine, tree_spruce; pyrenees: cliff, farmhouse, rock_a, rock_b, tree_pine; alps: church, cliff, farmhouse, rock_a, tree_spruce; city: building_block_a/b, building_oldtown, building_shop, building_tall, tree_beech (full table in data/scenery.json; lateral offsets up to 170 m for wind turbines, so props stand on TerrainProfile heights) -> PropLibrary mesh per set id, billboard of the same set as far LOD and as stand-in, lights layer -> window emission. Landmarks: 61 placements of 42 sets in 55 cities, up to 180 m beside the road, own haze law, far pass to 1,900 m, floodlight at night, procedural stand-ins (lattice tower, TV tower, wheel, column, octagon, campanile, dome, parliament, palace, atomium, lighthouse with rotating beams, skyscrapers) -> LandmarkLayer with true positions along the path, landmark shader, billboard beyond ~600 m. Signs: limit, unlimited, radar, fuel 30/15/5 km, fuel_lane, town, town_ahead, distance, border, tunnel, autobahn, autobahn_end, curve, crest, chevron, start gantry, finish gantry, per-country colours, wall-mounted variants -> SignAtlas. Procedural objects: streetlight, fuel_pylon, pump, station, radar camera (flash with radar_flash01), booth, truss portal, pylon, bridge lamp -> meshes with emissive parts.

INVENTORY D, vehicles and lights -> 3D. Player (5 cars; visible yaw from curve preview, steer, lateral speed, understeer; roll <= 2.5 deg; brake and tail layers; blinking while invulnerable; shake) -> hero meshes with pose terms, emissive lights, spot headlights, shadow. Traffic (33 sets: hatch, sedan, wagon, suv, van, sports in colours; truck and bus as textured boxes; yaw smoothing and flank warp; tail lights at night and in tunnels; brake lights; indicators announcing lane changes; spray in rain; wet reflections; soft shadow under boxes) -> meshes with paint colour per instance and light slots; smoothing and warp become unnecessary. Police (18 liveries, beacon phases a/b, blue glow, chase overlay blue/red at the screen corners, radar chase) -> one body + 18 livery textures, beacon emission + pooled blue omni, overlay stays a 2D canvas effect. risks: Terrain and horizon closure in true 3D is the largest visual risk: ribbon edges, the far ground on the outside of climbing bends and the hole at the centre of tight bends are visible in the spike (pair_sp198_1_narrow_ribbon.png, pair_sp172_1.png). Mitigation: wide rings where the clearance table allows, far-ground plane, fog, backdrop on the true horizon, roadside vegetation; fallback: the sheared mapping behind RoadPath3D.

Steam Deck GPU performance is inferred, not measured: there is no GPU here (llvmpipe). Shadows, MSAA and alpha-tested foliage overdraw are the unknowns. Mitigation: presets with hard proxy budgets, render scale, an early test build on a real Deck.

Fairness can regress through art, not code: terrain relief or dense vegetation on the inside of bends, darker nights, bloom, small indicators. Mitigation: the rule set in the decisions and the two headless fairness tests using the shipped terrain and camera parameters; they must run in tools/run_tests.sh.

Future stages may loop inside the loaded window (two same-direction curviness-3 curves can turn 312 degrees within about 1.3 km in theory; today the minimum is 267.6 m clearance and loops need >= 2,544 m of path). Mitigation: validator test, seed change for new stages, runtime clamp of the terrain width.

Literal fairness ('visible at least as early as in Arcade') does not hold in true 3D: beyond 270 m in the tightest bends Arcade still shows vehicles at the screen edge that 3D has outside the frustum, and 1.28 % of crest targets are seen later (never inside the stopping sight distance). If the lead or user insists on the literal reading, only the sheared world model satisfies it.

Compatibility renderer limits: 8 lights per object and 32 renderable lights by default, no SSR/SSAO/volumetric fog, probably no cross-fade for LOD ranges, behaviour of BG_CANVAS, depth fog and SubViewport textures on ANGLE (Windows) verified only on Mesa here. Mitigation: pooled lights and shader pools, hard LOD switches hidden by fog, Wine smoke test, automatic fallback to Arcade.

Two renderers must show every gameplay-relevant element. Anything added later (a new sign kind, a new structure) has to be implemented twice; forgetting one is a fairness bug. Mitigation: the element lists come from Track (shared), a checklist test that every sign kind and prop kind of Track is known to both renderers.

Hitches: Track generation already peaks at 6–10 ms per 96 m in the sim step; a chunk commit in the same frame adds 1–3 ms (more on the Deck). Mitigation: threaded build, one commit per frame, skip the commit in frames where the Track generated, pre-rendered sign textures.

Engine quirks cost calibration time: directional light acts about pi times stronger than expected, two-sided materials flip normals of back faces (the first spike frames were wrongly lit), ViewportTextures have no mipmaps. Each needs a render check so it cannot regress silently.

The look-into-the-curve camera puts the player car up to 135 px off-centre and rotates the world; feel and motion comfort are untested with a human player. Mitigation: gain as a setting, 'Kamera: klassisch' option, playtest on the vertical slice.

Asset volume: meshes with LODs for 5 player cars, 8 traffic bodies, 18 police liveries, 86 props and 33 landmarks must stay inside the archive limit (today 127 MB, limit about 350 MB); the billboard far-LOD reuses the existing 70 MB of sprites, which helps, but the Arcade sprites cannot be removed.

result.summary:
ENGINE CAPABILITY PROBE – Godot 4.7.2, Compatibility renderer (Mesa 25.2 llvmpipe under Xvfb: desktop GL 4.5 core, plus the GLES 3.2 path that ANGLE would translate; exported Linux release build; Windows export under wine64/WGL). About 60 small experiments, each with screenshots, image diffs against a baseline and render counters. The repo is untouched (git status clean; only git-ignored Python bytecode caches under tools/blender/cesprites/__pycache__ were refreshed by one exploratory import). Scratch is reduced to 12 MB of evidence.

RESULT: the lead's hypothesis holds. A real-3D "Modern" renderer in the same build on the Compatibility renderer is feasible, and Arcade is not disturbed: in a scratch copy of the game the Arcade race frame was bit-identical (max diff 0) before and after a 3D scene with shadows, glow, MSAA 4x and 3D scaling ran in the same session.

WORKS (screenshot per item, see evidence):
- Sun shadows: orthogonal, PSSM 2/4 splits, split blending, filter quality 0-5, atlas 1024-8192. The first shadowed directional light is drawn in the base pass, so it costs only the caster draws.
- Omni, spot and the new AreaLight3D; omni/spot shadows.
- Emissive materials with glow; tonemappers linear/Reinhard/filmic/ACES/AgX with exposure and white; brightness/contrast/saturation; 1D and 3D LUT colour correction.
- Fog: exponential, depth mode, height fog, sun scatter, aerial perspective.
- SSAO (a simple depth-only AO with 5 quality levels) – supported in Compatibility in this version.
- MSAA 3D; bilinear and nearest 3D scaling from 0.5 to 2.0.
- ProceduralSky and a custom sky shader (fbm clouds, stars, sun/moon disc, own dithering); sky radiance as ambient and reflections.
- ReflectionProbe (UPDATE_ONCE, box projection); a custom screen-space reflection overlay for a wet road, written with the screen and depth textures.
- Alpha blend, depth pre-pass, refraction, alpha scissor (also with alpha-to-coverage).
- GPUParticles3D and CPUParticles3D for rain, snow, spray, sparks.
- MultiMesh with 20,000 instances in 1 draw call; alpha-scissor foliage casts silhouette shadows.
- Custom spatial shaders with vertex displacement (world bending), global shader parameters and per-instance uniforms; shadows follow the bent geometry when the bend origin comes from a global uniform.
- Visibility ranges, automatic mesh LOD (at glTF import and at runtime via ImporterMesh.generate_lods), occlusion culling.
- 2D/3D mixing: CanvasLayer HUD over 3D; a 2D canvas as the 3D background (BG_CANVAS); 3D SubViewport inside a 2D menu (transparent background, own world, MSAA); full-screen canvas post shader on the screen texture (vignette, radial blur, droplets, chromatic aberration); full-screen 3D quad with depth-texture access; HDR 2D with 2D glow.
- Text signs: 2D drawing in a SubViewport used as ViewportTexture or mipmapped ImageTexture on quads; Label3D.
- glTF from Blender 5.2: hierarchy and names (wheels are separate nodes), base colour, metallic, roughness, emission; LODs, shadow meshes and attribute compression are generated at import. S3TC/BPTC textures load.
- Linux and Windows exports run the full smoke scene.

WORKS WITH LIMITS (all found by experiment):
1. Positional lights: 8 omni + 8 spot per mesh instance and 32 in total. Beyond that, lights drop out arbitrarily – a 1400 m road mesh went dark near the camera with 9 lamps. Fixes that worked: road chunks of 25 m, distance fade on the lights, or raised limits (startup project settings).
2. Every shadowed light is added to the picture in sRGB-encoded space (visible in the embedded shader source and measured: 47 + 92 = 139 instead of 103), so lit areas get brighter as soon as a light casts shadows.
3. Glow, adjustments, SSAO or 3D scale other than 1.0 switch tonemapping from the material shader to a post pass; with a shadowed light the picture then changes (grass 135,249,121 becomes 140,225,128).
4. BG_COLOR / clear-colour backgrounds come out 4x too bright when glow is on (205 instead of 51). Sky and BG_CANVAS backgrounds are fine.
5. ReflectionProbe UPDATE_ALWAYS stays black, or stale if switched from ONCE (120 frames tested). UPDATE_ONCE works and re-captures in 2-8 frames when the probe is moved.
6. PhysicalSkyMaterial renders very dark at the default energy multiplier with sun energy 1.3; raising it changes the picture.
7. GPU particles: no trails, sub-emitters or manual emit; they cast shadows by default.
8. Visibility-range fade and GeometryInstance3D.transparency are ignored (hard pop).
9. Imported vertex colours arrive, but the material flag vertex_color_use_as_albedo is not set.
10. Shader variants compile on first use: 0.5-1.9 s hitch per new feature on llvmpipe with cold caches. Variants depend on which light types touch an object, fog mode, PSSM mode, filter quality and probes. Replaying identical state combinations in the main viewport removes the hitches; rendering everything once with all features on does not.
11. The separate render thread is flagged experimental by the engine itself.
12. World bending needs tessellated meshes and cull margins; a blanket 2000 m margin tripled the draw calls.
13. Today's traffic cars, trucks and buildings paint windows, lights and facades in procedural Blender shaders, so their glTF export is a featureless body. Player cars are fully modelled and export well, but are heavy (276k triangles, 93 objects).

UNAVAILABLE (engine warning plus zero image difference): Decal, volumetric fog / FogVolume, SSR, SSIL, SDFGI, TAA, FXAA, SMAA, FSR 1/2, debanding, glow levels/strength/blend modes, particle trails. Alpha hash is broken (opaque white quad). Per the docs and engine strings of this build, also DOF, auto exposure, light projectors, PCSS, VoxelGI and the Shader Baker. LightmapGI baking is impossible here (no RenderingDevice on this machine, and baking is an editor function).

NOT VERIFIABLE HERE: any real GPU timing, ANGLE/Direct3D 11 (Wine cannot run it), and Forward+/Mobile (no Vulkan driver: `--rendering-method forward_plus` falls back to OpenGL).
result.recommendation:
Stay on the Compatibility renderer for v0.8.0 and build "Modern" as a second, real-3D renderer in the same process.

Why Compatibility is enough: sun shadows, emissive + glow, tonemapping, LUT grading, fog, SSAO, MSAA, custom sky, sky and probe reflections, particles, MultiMesh, LOD, custom shaders and screen/depth post effects all work, and they run in the exported Linux build, in the Windows build under wine64 and on the GLES3 path. That is a clearly better picture than Arcade without leaving the renderer the game ships on.

Why not Forward+/Mobile now:
- It cannot be started on this machine at all (Vulkan init fails, the engine switches to OpenGL 3), so we would ship a renderer we never saw.
- The rendering method is fixed at process start, so a mode switch would need a restart. Arcade would either run on a different 2D backend (bit identity no longer guaranteed) or the game would have to relaunch itself.
- Machines without Vulkan/D3D12 fall back to OpenGL anyway, so the Compatibility path would still have to exist and be tested.
- What it would add, per this build's docs: SSR, SSIL, SDFGI/VoxelGI, volumetric fog, decals, light projectors, TAA/FSR2/FXAA/SMAA, DOF, auto exposure, PCSS, clustered lights without per-object limits, linear HDR lighting, particle trails and precompiled shaders (Forward+); Mobile adds decals, projectors and screen-space AA but has no SSAO. The official Windows template already references Vulkan and D3D12, so a later optional profile needs no new template – only real test hardware.

Design the Modern renderer around the engine limits found:
1. One shadowed light only (sun or moon); everything else unshadowed or faked. Shadowed lights add in sRGB space and cost an extra pass per object.
2. Keep the post path permanently on (glow always enabled) and never use BG_COLOR; use the sky shader or BG_CANVAS.
3. Chunk road and terrain into pieces of 25 m or less; manage lights with a budget and distance fade.
4. Fix fog mode, PSSM mode and shadow filter quality per quality preset, and pre-warm shaders by replaying the real state combinations in the main viewport behind a loading overlay.
5. Rebuild decals as quads or in the road shader; use alpha scissor (not alpha hash) for foliage; use UPDATE_ONCE probes re-triggered by script, or the custom wet-road reflection shader.
6. Treat the draw-call count as the main CPU budget on the Deck: about 1,200-1,500 per frame including shadow passes (inferred from 2-5 µs per call measured here). GPU cost must be measured on a real Deck before release.
decisions: Renderer: Compatibility for both modes, switch at runtime without restart. Evidence: scratch copy of the game ran race (2D) -> 3D scene (shadows, glow, fog, MSAA 4x, scaling 0.75, changed shadow atlas) -> race again; the Arcade frames were bit-identical (max diff 0, control run also 0), no errors, 0 orphan nodes.

Modern must never touch project-wide 2D state. Viewport.use_hdr_2d stays off; MSAA 3D, 3D scaling, shadow atlas sizes and filter quality are set at runtime on entering Modern and reset on leaving (this is what the switch test did). Raising rendering/limits/opengl/* is a startup setting that does not affect 2D.

Exactly one shadow-casting light (sun by day, moon by night). Reason: the first shadowed directional light is drawn in the base pass (495 -> 695 draw calls with orthogonal shadows = casters only); a second shadowed directional light added a full extra pass (1493 draw calls). Shadowed omni/spot lights always get an additive pass per object, and omni shadows are 6-face cubes (dual paraboloid is refused).

Accept, and tune the art for, sRGB-space addition of shadowed lights. The embedded GLES3 scene shader converts the base and the shadowed-light term to sRGB separately and adds them; measured ambient 47 + sun 92 = 139 with the shadow on versus 103 with it off. Do not use shadow on/off as a quality toggle without a calibrated compensation of energy or ambient.

Keep the post path permanently on in Modern (glow always enabled, intensity may be near 0). Glow, adjustments, SSAO and 3D scale other than 1.0 each move tonemapping into a post pass and change the picture when a shadowed light is present (grass 135,249,121 -> 140,225,128); MSAA and HDR 2D do not. With the post path fixed, quality toggles no longer change the look.

Never use BG_COLOR or BG_CLEAR_COLOR in Modern. With glow on the background came out 4x too bright (51,64,77 -> 205,255,255), most likely because the clear colour is not scaled by the luminance multiplier. Use a sky shader, or BG_CANVAS with the existing 2D backdrop (tested with fog, glow and MSAA; the canvas background kept its brightness).

Own sky shader instead of PhysicalSkyMaterial. The custom shader (gradient, fbm clouds, stars, sun/moon disc and halo from LIGHT0, own dithering because debanding is ignored) rendered correctly and feeds ambient and reflections; PhysicalSkyMaterial came out very dark at its defaults. Do not use TIME in the sky shader if sky light is used: the docs say it forces a radiance update every frame; drive the cloud offset by a uniform updated a few times per second.

Road, terrain and long props in chunks of 25 m or less, and tessellated. Per-object light limit: a single 1400 m road mesh lost its near lighting with 9 lamps; 25 m chunks with 30 lamps were lit correctly. If world bending is used, vertex displacement needs vertices: a 700 m guard-rail box stayed a straight line.

Light budget manager plus distance fade. At most 32 positional lights are rendered by default and with 64 present the engine did not keep the nearest ones (near road dark). With distance_fade_enabled (begin 120 m, length 30 m) the near lamps stayed lit. Raising the limits to 128 total / 32 per object also worked. Traffic headlights and tail lights are emissive geometry with glow plus additive light-pool quads, not real lights.

Decals are replaced by alpha-blended quads 1-2 cm above the road (arrows, skid marks, additive light pools – tested) or, better, by markings drawn in the road shader. The Decal node is refused by the engine and changed nothing in the picture.

Foliage and fences use alpha scissor (optionally alpha-to-coverage with MSAA) or depth pre-pass; never alpha hash. Alpha hash rendered an opaque white quad in both tests; alpha scissor works in MultiMesh and casts silhouette shadows.

Reflections: sky radiance for car paint and wet road as the base. For objects use a ReflectionProbe in UPDATE_ONCE that the script nudges every N frames (re-capture visible after 2-8 frames; cull mask to limit what it renders; maximum 2 probes per mesh). UPDATE_ALWAYS is unusable (black after 120 frames). For wet-road light streaks use the custom screen-space reflection overlay; the prototype works, also with MSAA 4x.

Weather: GPUParticles3D for rain and snow with cast_shadow off (8000 rain quads added 65,200 shadow primitives by default), no trails or sub-emitters. CPUParticles3D only for small effects (measured main-thread cost 0.67 ms for 2000, 2.5 ms for 8000, 12.7 ms for 30,000 rain particles). Droplets, speed blur and vignette as a canvas post shader on a layer below the HUD.

LOD strategy: rely on automatic mesh LOD (20 sedans went from about 777k to about 52k triangles at the default 1 px threshold; a 4 px threshold showed visible faceting) plus visibility ranges for hard swaps to simple far versions. Cross-fades are not available, so choose swap distances where fog hides the pop.

Anti-aliasing is MSAA 3D only (FXAA, SMAA, TAA and FSR are refused). Offer 3D resolution scale (bilinear, 0.5-1.0) as the performance lever and supersampling above 1.0 for strong PCs. Both work together with glow and with screen/depth-reading shaders.

Shader hitches: per quality preset keep fog mode, sun scatter, PSSM mode, split blending and shadow filter quality constant for the whole session, and pre-warm behind the loading overlay by replaying the actual state combinations in the main viewport. Evidence: replay pass 1 had 0.46-1.78 s hitches per feature, pass 2 at most 72 ms (138 ms for the first upload of the 276k-triangle car). Rendering everything once with all features on did not help (hitches 0.14-1.37 s remained).

Rendering stays on the main thread. The engine prints that the separate render thread is experimental and may crash. Draw calls are therefore the CPU budget next to GDScript; target about 1,200-1,500 per frame including shadow passes for the Deck preset. A vehicle should be at most 4-6 surfaces plus wheels; the raw exports (sedan 24 objects, sports car 93 objects / 106 surfaces) are far above that, and merging by object alone only went from 42 to 35 draws per car.
One shared paint shader with per-instance uniforms for vehicle colour and light state (works: 6 boxes, one material, different colours and emission) instead of one material per colour variant.

Vehicle and prop assets come from the existing Blender generators as .glb, with an explicit material-mapping step. Player cars export complete; traffic cars, trucks, buses and buildings lose windows, lights and facades because those live in procedural Blender shaders, so they need real geometry or baked textures (the user asked for finer models anyway). Size is no obstacle: imported scenes are already compressed (gzip gains under 1%) and add about 1:1 to the archive.

Signs with text reuse SignPainter: draw in a 2D SubViewport once, snapshot to an ImageTexture with mipmaps (ViewportTexture has none) and put it on a quad; Label3D is available for simple cases. Both rendered correctly.

Stage coordinates must be rebased around the camera. A 400 km stage is 40 km of visible road; shifting the test scene by 40 km and 200 km already changed edges in a still frame (PSNR 41 dB and 37 dB), and float spacing is about 4 mm at 40 km. Moving chunk nodes is cheap (0.18-0.23 µs per node transform).
plan: 0. Kern (owner of project.godot, scripts/core): add Settings.graphics_mode ('arcade' | 'modern', default arcade) and graphics_quality; CLI switch --graphics=modern for tests; project.godot gets rendering/limits/opengl/max_renderable_lights=64 only if the light budget needs it. Do not enable hdr_2d, project-level MSAA or scaling. Export presets stay as they are (imported .glb scenes are covered by all_resources).

1. Renn-Modul, new folder scripts/race3d/ with one entry class ModernRenderer (Node3D) offering the same contract as RoadRenderer: setup(track, projection, cfg, scenery_db) and render(view) with the existing view dictionary. RaceSession picks the renderer from Settings.graphics_mode; simulation, HUD and audio hooks are unchanged. On enter it applies the viewport state (msaa_3d, scaling_3d_scale, shadow atlas and filter through RenderingServer); on exit it restores the defaults.

2. scripts/race3d/environment_rig.gd (can start immediately, owner: one agent): builds the WorldEnvironment – sky ShaderMaterial or BG_CANVAS, glow always enabled, fog always enabled with a density from the palette, tonemap, adjustments and optional LUT. Interface: apply(palette, weather, hour, in_tunnel). Shaders in assets/shaders/modern/sky.gdshader; starting point is evidence/prototypes/sky_clouds.gdshader.

3. scripts/race3d/light_rig.gd (parallel to step 2): one DirectionalLight3D for sun/moon with shadow settings per preset, player headlights as 1-2 unshadowed SpotLight3D, a pooled set of OmniLight3D for street and tunnel lamps with distance fade and a hard budget (at most 8 per 25 m chunk, 24 active). Interface: set_time(palette), place_lamps(list of positions), set_headlights(on).

4. scripts/race3d/chunk_streamer.gd (parallel, depends only on Track): generates road, shoulder, terrain and guard-rail chunks of 25 m or less as ArrayMesh from TrackSegment data ahead of the camera and frees them behind; rebases the origin around the camera; road markings in the road shader (assets/shaders/modern/road.gdshader). The lead must first decide between a true 3D path and the world-bending shader (evidence/prototypes/bend.gdshader); the interface is the same either way: update(camera_z, visibility_m).

5. scripts/race3d/vehicle_pool.gd (parallel, needs the asset contract from step 9): instances vehicle scenes by set id, maps view['cars'] entries to transforms, spins and steers wheel nodes, sets paint and light state through per-instance shader parameters (assets/shaders/modern/vehicle.gdshader), switches shadow casting off beyond the shadow distance and shows a blob-shadow quad instead.

6. scripts/race3d/scenery_pool.gd (parallel): props, trees and buildings from TrackSegment.sprites as MultiMesh chunks (alpha scissor foliage shader), landmarks as single instances with visibility ranges, signs through the existing SignPainter rendered once in a SubViewport and cached as mipmapped ImageTexture on quads.

Warmup replays every material in every light combination of the preset (no positional light, omni, spot, both; with and without probe) in the main viewport behind the loading overlay before the countdown.

9. Sprites module (owner of tools/blender, parallel from day one): tools/blender/export_models.py driven by the existing catalog, an explicit material table in cesprites/materials.py (base colour, metallic, roughness, emission group: tail, brake, head, blink, beacon), merging to at most 4-6 surfaces per vehicle plus wheel nodes, decimated player cars, new geometry or baked textures for traffic cars, trucks, buses and buildings. Output to assets/models/**.glb with committed .import settings (LODs and shadow meshes on) and a manifest with sizes, triangle and surface counts.

UI module (parallel): options entry 'Grafik: Arcade / Modern' and quality, German texts via tr(); a 3D showroom in the vehicle menu as a SubViewport with its own world and transparent background (pattern proven in t_2d.gd test_subviewport); for 16:10 screens decide whether Modern uses stretch aspect expand (3D fills 1280x800; HUD anchors must adapt).

11. Tests (Kern + Renn-Modul): headless logic tests for chunk streaming, pools and the light budget; Xvfb picture checks for Modern scenarios; counter assertions with Viewport.get_render_info (draw calls and primitives per scenario against the budget); the Arcade identity check from evidence/prototypes/game_switch_test.gd as a permanent test; export smoke runs for the Linux build, the Windows build under wine64 and the opengl3_es driver.

12. Docs in German: docs/grafik-modern.md with the engine limits from this probe (lights, shadowed-light brightness, post path, background rule, probes, shader warm-up), the presets and a troubleshooting section; update docs/steam-deck.md and docs/windows.md once real-device results exist.
risks: GPU performance is unmeasured. Everything ran on llvmpipe (CPU rasteriser); frame times there are dominated by vertex processing and are noisy (four other agents on 4 cores, roughly +/-20%). Draw calls, primitives and script times are real measurements; the Steam Deck budget (about 1,200-1,500 draw calls, MSAA 2-4x, 2 splits at 2048) is inferred. A real Deck run is needed before release; ship a benchmark switch and conservative Deck defaults.

ANGLE / Direct3D 11 on Windows is unverified for 3D. Wine cannot run ANGLE; only the GLES 3.2 path on Mesa was tested (full smoke scene rendered correctly). Machines that Godot forces onto ANGLE (older Intel HD, Radeon R5/R7/R9) could show driver-specific problems with shadow samplers, MSAA or float buffers.

Three of the limits look like engine defects rather than design (BG_COLOR 4x too bright with glow, ReflectionProbe UPDATE_ALWAYS black, alpha hash white). They are engine logic, so they should behave the same on real GPUs, but that is not proven here, and an engine update could change them. Workarounds must sit in one place each.

Lighting is not physically linear. Shadowed lights add in sRGB space and the post path changes the result, so day/night transitions and any preset that toggles shadows need per-preset tuning; copying Arcade palette values 1:1 will not match.

First-run shader stutter. With cold caches each new shader variant cost 0.5-1.9 s on llvmpipe; real drivers are faster but still stutter. If the warm-up misses a state combination (first lamp in range, first tunnel, rain starting), the player sees a hitch in the race. The warm-up list must be generated from the same code paths the race uses.

Draw-call budget against richer models. Rendering runs on the main thread; raw exports are 35-42 draws per traffic car and over 100 surfaces for a player car. Without the merge and surface-reduction step in the asset pipeline, 30 visible vehicles alone would exceed the budget.

Asset effort is larger than a pure export. Traffic cars, trucks, buses and buildings carry their detail in procedural Blender shaders, which glTF cannot transport; they need new geometry or texture baking. This is the largest work item and determines how good Modern looks.

World bending, if chosen, fights the engine's culling, shadow cascades and light pairing: a blanket cull margin tripled the draw calls and raised shadow primitives from 0.42M to 1.9M. A true 3D path avoids that but can make the road cross itself on tight curve sequences. Either choice needs a spike on real track data.

Per-object limits also apply to MultiMesh (one instance = one object: 8 lights for the whole forest chunk, shadow pass redraws all instances per cascade: 20,000 trees gave 372k shadow primitives). MultiMesh chunks must be small and far chunks must not cast shadows.

Archive size grows about 1:1 with model data because imported scenes are already compressed: roughly 6.8 MB per current player car, about 1 MB per traffic or police car, 0.7 MB for a landmark like the Eiffel tower. An estimated 80-100 MB of models would bring the archives to about 210-230 MB (limit 350 MB) – acceptable, but only with decimation and shared geometry across colour and livery variants.
Compatibility has no debanding and only 8-bit output without the post path; gradients (sky, fog, headlight falloff) need shader dithering, as done in the sky prototype.

PSNR between the Linux export and the Wine run was low (16-19 dB) because the Wine window rendered at a slightly different client size and rain is random; the pictures match visually, but pixel-exact cross-platform checks for Modern are not realistic.
open_questions: Road geometry: true 3D path (engine culling, shadows and lights work naturally, but the camera really turns and tight curve sequences could self-intersect) or world bending in the vertex shader (keeps the Arcade road-coordinate logic and occlusion behind crests, but needs cull margins, script-placed lights and tessellation)? Both are technically possible; this decides the structure of chunk_streamer.gd.
Traffic vehicles and buildings: model real geometry for windows and lights (finer models, more Blender work) or bake the existing procedural materials to textures (faster, lower fidelity up close)?

Is a real Steam Deck or any real-GPU test available before release? Without it the Deck preset (MSAA level, shadow splits, 3D scale) is a guess; alternatively ship Modern with conservative defaults and a built-in benchmark that the user runs once.
Can someone run the Windows build on real hardware, including a machine that falls back to ANGLE? If not, should Modern be hidden or marked experimental when the log shows the ANGLE driver?

Background for the first Modern version: reuse the existing 2D backdrop through BG_CANVAS (cheap, consistent with Arcade landscapes, no sky reflections from it) or go straight to the sky shader with 3D horizon silhouettes?
Should Modern fill 16:10 screens (stretch aspect expand, HUD re-anchored) or keep the 16:9 picture with bars like Arcade?

Is an optional Forward+ profile wanted later (SSR, volumetric fog, decals, TAA)? If yes, shaders and scene code should avoid Compatibility-only assumptions from the start; if no, workarounds can be simpler.

result.summary:
Design + spikes for the Modern-mode asset pipeline; repo untouched (git status clean), everything in the scratch folder, large copies deleted (27 MB of evidence kept).

FINDINGS
1. The procedural Blender generators already build complete real-scale 3D models; the sprites are only one rendering of them. I built every generator once and measured it: 155 distinct models = 2.96 M triangles after modifiers (player cars 276–323k each, traffic cars/van 38–45k, trucks 9–13k, bus 8.4k, police 40–43k, trees 0.5–7.7k, rural buildings 68–1,640, city buildings 222–23k with a median of 3k, landmarks 0.4–25k). All generators together build in about 9 minutes.
2. Geometry survives an export (only BEVEL/SUBSURF/SOLIDIFY/DISPLACE/SHRINKWRAP modifiers, text is already mesh, no curve objects are left). Materials do not: 95% of the player-car triangles carry flat Principled colours (fine), but 91% of the traffic-car triangles and practically all facades, trees and landmarks carry object-space mask or noise shaders, which Blender's stock glTF exporter turns into a white base colour with emissive [1,1,1].
3. A prototype exporter (scratch package ce3d, about 1,300 lines: evaluated meshes -> own GLB writer, surfaces by role, Cycles EMIT bakes into a box-unwrapped atlas incl. emission layers and cut-out opacity, automatic shader-decal -> geometry conversion, LOD through generator parameters) exported 13 representative assets with the real generators: player car, traffic sedan (baked and geometry variant), truck, bus, police car, two city blocks, four landmarks, oak (sprite model and two card variants). All import into a scratch Godot 4.7.2 project and render under the Compatibility renderer (opengl3 on llvmpipe/Xvfb) with sun shadows by day and, at night, emissive tail/brake/beacon lamps, lit windows, flood-lit landmarks, shadowed spot-light headlights and glow. Node names, pivots and glTF extras arrive intact.
4. A sweep of the prototype over the whole catalog exported 152 of 155 models; the three failures are the atlas packer running out of space at the 256 px test size for lattice models with 6k–12k charts (Eiffel tower, Riesenrad, Cologne cathedral – the first and the last export fine at 2048 px, and such models belong on the vertex-colour bake, which I verified separately).
5. What the spikes decided: decimating finished cars destroys them (stacked decal patches), generator-level detail does not (281k -> 100k / 50k / 29k, all clean); baked atlases are right for buildings and landmarks but too soft for cars, where converting the shader decals into geometry gives crisp cars with no textures and free colour variants; the sprite trees are blob lollipops in real time, leaf-card trees look right at 1.3–1.8k triangles; trucks and buses already are real models.
6. Problems found and solved or scoped: decals z-fight beyond roughly 100 m with a 0.3 m near plane, MultiMesh cannot mirror single instances, the generators are modelled for the sprite view (blank back walls, crude traffic fronts, smeared wrap-around lamps), 25 models use cut-out materials, two use fake light volumes, 1-sample bakes alias on brick, name-based grouping is fragile.

Measured vs. inferred: triangle, draw-call, byte and time figures are measured here; frame times on a real GPU / the Steam Deck are not measurable on llvmpipe and are only inferred from those proxies.
result.recommendation:
The lead's hypothesis holds for the assets, with four corrections: (1) Blender's stock glTF exporter is not usable – use an own small GLB writer with three material translation paths; (2) LODs must come from generator detail levels, never from decimating finished cars; (3) vegetation has to be rebuilt as card foliage, the sprite models are not good enough in real time; (4) trucks and buses need no new modelling to become real models, only articulation nodes and a finer cab.

Build one generic pipeline, tools/blender/ce3d + export_all.py, that drives the existing generators and writes assets/models/**.glb, textures and assets/models/manifest.json:
- flat colours -> one vertex-PBR surface per node (no texture);
- named role surfaces (paint, glass, lens, lamp_*, leaves ...) that the renderer binds to its own shaders;
- procedural shaders -> decal geometry for all vehicles, baked S3TC atlases or vertex-colour bakes for static props.
Add a validator with per-category budgets and Godot-rendered contact sheets.

Expected cost: about 25–35 MB of meshes and 190–230 MB of S3TC atlases in the pck, which is about +80–95 MB in the release archives (about 200–222 MB before the audio additions, limit 350 MB). Cold export of the whole set takes about 1–3 hours in one process (cached, incremental afterwards).

Build the core module first (it fixes the interfaces), then player cars, traffic/police, heavy vehicles, vegetation, buildings and landmarks in parallel.
decisions: Own GLB writer instead of Blender's glTF exporter. Evidence: the stock export of sedan / Gruenderzeit block / oak / truck keeps the triangles (38,844 / 2,822 / 5,900 / 11,792) but writes one node per object (25–36 nodes) and loses every mask or noise material (sedan: body, cabin, bumper = 91% of the triangles come out white with emissive [1,1,1]; block 5 of 10 materials; oak 2 of 2). The 157-line numpy writer (ce3d/glb.py) writes merged, named nodes and role surfaces in 0.1–1.7 s per asset; Godot 4.7.2 imports it without errors and keeps node names, pivots and extras (as metadata).

Surfaces are roles, not source materials. All flat Principled materials of a node merge into one surface 'trim' with COLOR_0 = albedo (sRGB bytes) and UV0 = (roughness, metallic): no texture, one draw call (player/kompakt: 47 source materials -> 9 body surfaces + 1 per wheel). Fixed vocabulary: paint, paint2, paint3 (livery colours), trim, glass, lens, lamp_tail, lamp_brake, lamp_tailbrake, lamp_reverse, lamp_ind_l, lamp_ind_r, lamp_head, lamp_drl, lamp_plate, lamp_marker, lamp_beacon_a, lamp_beacon_b, baked, baked_cutout, leaves, bark, merged. The renderer assigns its own materials by role name, so paint colour, clear coat and the 26 traffic colour sets are material parameters on 6 meshes. Generators must tag objects and materials with custom properties (ce_node, ce_role): name matching was fragile in the spike (a lamp patch named *_brake1 landed in a wheel node).

Lamps: one surface per lamp role with the unlit colour in COLOR_0 and emission colour and strength per sprite layer (tail, brake, beacon_a, beacon_b, lights) in the material extras – parsed automatically from the CE_PASS node trees. Merged far LODs carry a lamp role code in COLOR_0.a instead. The manifest lists light anchors (role, position, size, colour) so the renderer can place spot lights and far glow sprites and keep lights visible at least as early as in Arcade. The fake light volumes of the sprite scenes (streetlight sl_cone, fuel station fs_haze) are exported as light points, not as geometry.

LODs come from generator detail parameters; finished patch-built cars are never decimated. Evidence: planar dissolve at 1 degree cuts player/kompakt from 280,822 to 82,687 triangles but the paint breaks through the side glass, 3 degrees and collapse are worse (shots/_cmp_kompakt_lods.png). Coarser lofts, patch grids and wheel segments inside the generator give 99,616 / 49,984 / 29,036 triangles with windows, seams, plate and lamps intact (shots/_cmp_kompakt_detail.png). Rule: decals are always cast onto the final body of that LOD. Godot's automatic LOD stays on for large LOD0 meshes as a bonus (99.6k-triangle car: 43.7k rendered at 4.5 m, 14.6k at 150 m).

All vehicles except the player cars (traffic cars, van, police, trucks, buses): the shader decals (windows, lamps, plates, seams, handles, cladding) are converted automatically into geometry – one constrained Delaunay triangulation per projection face, ray-cast onto the body, top-most decal wins – with no textures. Evidence: the prototype ce3d/decalgeo.py converts all six car designs without touching designs.py (2.5–4.2 s each); the sedan is clean and crisp at 39,757 triangles with a uniform 1.6 cm grid, has a few specks at the tight lamp corner at 21,928 triangles (3 cm grid), lamps are separate emissive surfaces and any paint colour works. The baked alternative (1024 px atlas with paint mask) shows wavy edges and colour fringes (shots/_sheet_vehicles.png, _cmp_sedan_lamps.png). Still to do in production: adaptive decal grid (a uniform 2 cm grid costs 14–32k decal triangles; target 6k or less) and a far LOD that classifies the faces of a coarse body instead of using patches.

Static props (buildings, landmarks, rocks, road furniture): geometry as generated plus baked textures – box unwrap (six axis charts per connected component), shelf packing, Cycles EMIT bakes of base colour, roughness/metallic, the emission layer 'lights' and opacity for cut-out materials, with visibility-weighted texel density (road and approach faces 1.0, away faces 0.3, undersides 0.05). Evidence: Gruenderzeit block (2,822 triangles + atlas) holds up at 10 m and shows lit windows at night; Haussmann block with wrought-iron railings as alpha cut-outs; Michel, Cologne cathedral and Eiffel tower flood-lit (shots/_sheet_environment.png, haussmann_close.png, _cmp_cutout.png, _cmp_koelner_dom.png). Bake at twice the resolution with 16 samples and downsample, because 1-sample bakes alias on brick (shots/_cmp_bake_aa.png). Lattice-like models (Eiffel tower: 12,347 charts give only 2.4 px/m) bake to vertex colours instead (5.7 s per pass, verified).

Runtime texture format: VRAM-compressed S3TC (BC1 for albedo and emission, BC3 where alpha is needed) with mipmaps; tiers 2048x1024 for city-centre blocks, 1024 px for small houses and props, 2048 px for landmarks, emission at half size. Evidence for a 2048 px albedo: BC1 is 2.80 MB in the pck, 0.48–0.97 MB after gzip, 2.8 MB VRAM, 1–2.6 ms to load; lossy WebP is 0.08–0.28 MB but 22.4 MB VRAM and 43–53 ms; lossless 1.55–2.83 MB and about 110 ms; BPTC 5.59 MB; Basis-UASTC 1.16–1.68 MB and 61 ms. BC1 is visually equal to lossless on a facade at 10 m (shots/_cmp_bld_texfmt.png).

Vegetation is rebuilt for real time: trunk and branches from the existing helpers, a low-poly solid core, alpha-tested leaf cards placed on the crown blobs of the sprite model (same seeds, so the silhouette matches the sprite), shading normals pointing outward, wind weights in COLOR_0 (sway by height, phase per card), one leaf atlas of 256–512 px per species. LOD0 up to 2.5k triangles (0–50 m), LOD1 fewer and larger cards up to 900 (50–150 m), LOD2 a Y-billboard baked from the card tree, with the existing Arcade tree sprite as fallback. Evidence: card oak at 1,840 / 1,280 triangles next to the exported sprite model at 5,900 triangles, which reads as a blob lollipop (shots/oak_cards_day.png); the cards cast dappled shadows in the Compatibility renderer.

Trucks and buses become real models by exporting what the generators already build (truck 9.1–12.7k triangles with ten wheels, chassis, guards, tanks, lock rods and text; bus 8.4k with a lofted body) – shown lit by day and at night with the contour marking glowing. New work: nodes tractor and trailer with pivots at the kingpin, wheels per axle, decals -> geometry for cab glazing and lamps, a lofted cab instead of the bevelled box, two trailer meshes (box, tarp) plus text; liveries through paint/paint2/paint3 so the 4 + 3 variants share meshes. The footprint stays the collision box (2.55 m x 16.5 m and 12.8 m).

Conventions: metres. Generator space (x right, y forward along the road, z up) is written as glTF/Godot X = x, Y = z, Z = -y, so a vehicle nose and the far side of a prop point to -Z. Vehicles have their origin on the ground under the centre of the footprint (today the player models are centred and the traffic models rear-anchored – the exporter normalises), props at the sprite anchor (centre of the near face, trunk base). Nodes: model / lod0..2 / body, wheel_<axle><l|r> with the pivot at the wheel centre (spin about the car's X axis, front wheels steer about Y), hub_* for brake calipers (they must not spin; today they are part of the wheel mesh), tractor and trailer, shadow (low-poly caster). Left wheels are the right wheel turned 180 degrees, no negative scales. Manifest object sizes must equal the sprite manifest because both modes share the simulation.

What 'finer' means concretely. Player cars: transparent glass with a modelled interior (seats, headrests, dashboard, steering wheel, door cards; up to 6k triangles; new generator module), fixed calipers, real grille mesh instead of the object-space brick shader (it exported as blank patches), projector lenses, fixes for 3D views (wrap-around tail lamps smear onto the flank, mirror arms), a showroom mesh of about 100–120k and a race mesh of about 50k triangles. Traffic: geometry decals, real wheels with two or three rim styles, mirrors, seat and driver silhouettes behind tinted glass at LOD0, a plate atlas per country, better fronts. Environment: two to four times the texel density of the sprites, real relief that casts shadows, glass reflections, night windows, card foliage with wind, two seed variants per tree species.

Texel density with the recommended tiers (road-facing walls, measured): city blocks 26–34 px/m at 2048x1024 and 40–54 px/m at 2048 px (sprites today about 13 px/m), small houses 36–41 px/m at 1024 px (sprites 15–21), landmarks 6–15 px/m at 2048 px (sprites 2–6). For reference, the screen shows 47 px/m at 15 m and 4.7 px/m at 150 m at 1280 px width.

Godot import settings, written by a script and committed as .import files: meshes with generate_lods on for LOD0 meshes above 5k triangles, create_shadow_meshes off (explicit shadow node), ensure_tangents off (no normal maps on vertex-PBR meshes), compression on, light baking off; textures with compress/mode=2 (S3TC), mipmaps on, detect_3d off. Evidence on the 99.6k-triangle car: default import 2.76 MB, without LOD data 1.83 MB, without LOD data and shadow meshes 1.05 MB (10.5 bytes per triangle), uncompressed 1.24 MB.

Model manifest assets/models/manifest.json parallel to the sprite manifest. 'models': id -> file, kind, object, pivot, lods [node, tris, max_dist_m], wheels [node, pos, radius, steer], surfaces with roles and default colours, lights [role, pos, size, colour], textures (albedo, emission, orm), mirror, extent_m, tags, hash, bytes. 'sets': sprite set id -> model + variant + colours, so every id the simulation uses (traffic/sedan_red, police/de ...) resolves in both modes. Godot side: an autoload ModelDB mirroring SpriteDB; object_size must agree between the two.

Budgets enforced by the validator (triangles LOD0 / LOD1 / LOD2): player showroom 120k, race 55k, shadow caster 8k; traffic car 18k / 6k / 1.2k plus a 12-triangle box beyond 350 m, with at most 10 / 2 / 1 surfaces; truck and bus 25k / 7k / 1.5k; police = base car plus up to 4k for livery, words and light bar; tree 2.5k (up to 450 cards) / 900 / billboard; bush 400 / 120; rock 1.5k (cliff 6k); rural building 2k, city building 10k, landmark 25k, road furniture 1.5k (pylon 5k) as single LODs with Godot auto-LOD. Whole set: at most 35 MB of meshes and 240 MB of S3TC textures in the pck.

Depth rule for decals: patches hover 0.7–3 mm above the body. With a 0.3 m near plane they z-fight at 150 m (rear window and plate break up), with a 2 m near plane they are clean, and at 50 m both are clean (shots/_cmp_zfight.png). So: race camera near plane of 1.5 m or more, patch-carrying LODs only up to about 80 m, offsets scale with the LOD, far LOD without patches.

Mirrored placement: a MeshInstance3D with scale.x = -1 renders correctly, but a mirrored instance inside a MultiMesh renders inside-out (shots/mirror_test.png, mirror_multimesh.png). The exporter therefore writes a pre-mirrored mesh (node body_m) for props tagged mirror_left; landmarks are never mirrored but turned 180 degrees on the left side of the road.

Arcade stays byte-identical: all 3D code lives in the new package tools/blender/ce3d; changes inside cesprites are additive hooks whose defaults reproduce today's geometry (detail object, role tags, 3D-only fixes behind a flag); sprites are not re-rendered in v0.8.0 and validate_manifest.py keeps passing. The triangle counts and bounding boxes of all builds in out/inventory.json serve as a regression fixture.

Repository sources: .glb plus atlases as WebP at quality 95 (a 2048 px albedo is 0.13–0.32 MB instead of 1.0–2.3 MB as PNG); estimated growth of about 70 MB in git (about 48 MB meshes, 22 MB textures), comparable to the 70 MB of sprites today.
