Files: scripts/core/model_db.gd (autoload ModelDB: has_model(set_id), entry(set_id), instantiate(id, lod), mesh(id, lod, mirrored), textures(id), lights(id), object_size(set_id), preload); role shaders (trim, paint, glass, lens, lamp, baked, leaves, merged) – prototypes in godot_spike/shaders; tests/unit/core/test_model_db.gd incl. parity of object sizes and set ids with SpriteDB.

Integration and QA – all owners, coordinated by M0. validate_models.py checks: manifest against files, triangles per LOD and category, texture tiers and bytes, required nodes, roles and light anchors, object size against the sprite manifest within 2%, wheels on the ground, UVs inside 0..1, every sprite set mapped to a model or an explicit fallback. Then contact sheets for every model, size report of the import cache, cold and warm export times, German documentation.
risks: No GPU here. Everything was rendered on llvmpipe; triangle, draw-call and byte counts are measured, frame times on the Steam Deck are inferred. Alpha-tested foliage overdraw and the number of surfaces per near car are the open performance questions (spike scene with ten instances: 152k primitives and 136 draw calls per frame by day incl. four shadow splits; 315 draw calls at night with six shadowed spot lights).

The generators are modelled for the sprite view: traffic fronts are crude, building walls facing away from the road are blank (shots/_cmp_backsides.png), lamp patches cast from the rear smear around corners. If the Modern road is real curved geometry, blank walls become visible across bends. The wall-reuse trick and a per-model audit from several directions are in the plan, but fixes will cost time.

Decal patches can z-fight at distance and stacked layers interpenetrate. Mitigated by the single-layer triangulation, casting onto the final LOD body, a near plane of 1.5 m or more and patch-free far LODs; a cockpit or very close camera would additionally need a depth-biased decal shader.

Size creep: the S3TC atlases are 190–230 MB uncompressed in the pck. Together with about 30 MB of meshes and the audio additions the 350 MB archive limit holds only with the tiers above, so the validator must enforce the byte budget. The executable with embedded pck grows from 398 / 434 MB to roughly 620–710 MB.

Export time: supersampled bakes cost about 3 minutes per 2048 px asset (about 2.9 hours cold for all atlases in one process, about 1 hour with three workers); a police car costs 19 s even at 256 px because the bake overhead is per object and pass. Needs joined bake objects and a per-asset cache from day one.

New modelling code (interiors, card vegetation for nine species plus bushes, lofted truck cab, plate atlas) is the largest effort and the main schedule risk. Vegetation is not optional: the existing tree models are not acceptable in real time.

Touching shared generator modules can change sprite geometry by accident and would break the pixel-identical Arcade mode on the next sprite render. Mitigation: 3D code in its own package, hooks with unchanged defaults, the inventory as a regression fixture, no sprite re-render in v0.8.0.
BC1 shows banding on smooth gradients; acceptable on facades in the spike, but landmarks with large flat tints may need BC7 for a few assets (twice the size).
Windows/ANGLE and real-GPU behaviour of alpha scissor with MSAA, S3TC and 8-bit vertex colours is untested here; only Wine smoke tests are possible.
open_questions: Atlas format: S3TC with the recommended tiers (about +50 MB in the archive, 2.8 MB VRAM per 2048 px atlas, instant load) or lossy WebP (about +20 MB, but 22 MB VRAM per atlas and about 50 ms load each)? I recommend S3TC; the lead has to weigh it against the audio and music budget.
Interiors and transparent glass: only for the five player cars (recommended), also as silhouettes for traffic at LOD0, or not at all in v0.8.0?
Does the Modern renderer build real curved road geometry or bend the world like the pseudo-3D view? It decides whether blank building backs matter and how much all-round quality landmarks need.

Landmark wish list: about 20 cities still use procedural shapes or substitute sprites in Arcade. For Modern, build simple 3D shapes in the renderer, new Blender landmark models, or billboards of the Arcade drawing?
Is about 70 MB of committed .glb and WebP sources acceptable (same practice as the sprites today), or should models be generated at build time, which needs Blender and 1–3 hours for a cold run?
Player cars: separate showroom mesh (100–120k triangles) and race mesh (about 50k), as recommended, or one mesh of about 70k for both?

result.summary:
Study of the "Modern" audio profile (design + two spikes; repo untouched, git status clean; nobody could listen – every quality statement below is a measurement or an inference, marked as such).

WHAT MAKES TODAY'S SOUND "FLAT" (measured on the real game v0.7.0 with Movie Maker, Gran Turismo, autopilot race Hamburg–Hannover and a scripted drive):
1. Dull and band-limited: above ~5–6 kHz there is almost nothing (1/3-octave bands >= 6.3 kHz are 23–45 dB below the loudest band); the only high content is the turbo whistle, a pure 4.9 kHz sine that sticks out 10 dB above its neighbour bands. At 130 km/h the share above 5 kHz is -30 dB.
2. Static: at constant throttle the level varies by 0.22–0.46 dB (50-ms band level), a whole full-throttle run varies by 1.9 dB; the 8 cycle variants are only white-random, no slow life.
3. A drone at cruise: at 130 km/h in 7th gear one band (4th engine order, 167 Hz) lies 15–20 dB above every other band; there is no tyre layer for the own car at all and the wind is low-passed noise below 900 Hz (22 kHz SfxSynth).
4. Narrow: mono engine widened only by a short reverb (L/R correlation 0.73–0.95, idle 1.00).
5. Events have no body (shifts are only level dips, no tip-in transient), and the loudness plan is inconsistent: race about -13 LUFS, menu music -28.7 LUFS.
The physical bank model itself is good (exhaust orders, firing order, clips) – it is kept and extended, not replaced.

SPIKE 1 (engine, Gran Turismo, same drive as the game recording, level-matched in the full-throttle phase): prototype of the proposed runtime = stereo cycle bank built with the existing physical model (per-tailpipe panning, decorrelated flow noise, retuned rasp/jet/intake levels, stronger steepening), load attack/release, slow modulation, load-dependent saturation, biturbo as two narrow-band tones + flow hiss, blow-off with flutter, tip-in and driveline thumps, driveline whine, early reflections and a distant slap for the bangs, plus own tyres (left/right), three-band wind, expansion joints and pass-by whooshes. Result (old -> new complete): occupied 1/3-octave bands within 30 dB 21–26 -> 29 of 29; share >5 kHz at 130 km/h -30.3 -> -16.8 dB; L/R correlation 0.73–0.95 -> 0.57–0.76 (lift-off 0.43); steady-state modulation at 130 km/h 0.22 -> 0.60 dB; whistle spike gone; same loudness (-13.1 LUFS full throttle), true peak -0.75 dBTP. MP3/MP4 for the user are ready.

SPIKE 2 (music): (a) "remaster" of the title theme, bars 33–48, same notes, new production (layered kick/snare, sub bass, four guitar takes, wide lead double, deeper pump, new reverbs, multiband + M/S master): at equal loudness (-13.3 LUFS) sub 30–60 Hz -16.7 -> -9.5 dB, air >8 kHz -22.3 -> -17.1 dB, side/mid 2–8 kHz -4.4 -> -1.7 dB, PLR 11.9 -> 11.1, bass stays mono. (b) a new 36-s in-race track sketch "Linke Spur" (D minor, 132 bpm; count-in, groove with the brand's 3-3-2 motif, hook with harmony, ending): key detected D minor, all 16 chord roots right, -14.0 LUFS. (c) race-mix sketch: countdown, count-in lands on "Go", music 7.8 dB under the car (-24.0 vs -16.1 LUFS) with 4 dB sidechain ducking.

FEASIBILITY CHECKS (Godot 4.7.2 headless): stereo bank mixing costs about 1.0–1.15 ms per 1/60 s at 48 kHz in GDScript on this (loaded) machine, i.e. about 0.7 ms at 32 kHz (inferred) – too much for the Deck's main thread, but feeding the AudioStreamGenerator from a worker thread works (0 underruns with 400-ms main-thread hitches vs 535 on the main thread); int16 bank decode 1.6 M samples in 46 ms; AudioStreamInteractive switches clips gaplessly at clip end and at the next bar line; AudioEffectCompressor sidechain works but much stronger than its nominal ratio.
result.recommendation:
Build the Modern audio profile as a second, self-contained audio implementation next to today's (Arcade) one: AudioManager keeps its public API and only delegates to a new ModernAudio object when the profile is "modern"; no Arcade audio file, class or asset is edited or re-rendered. Modern consists of (1) engine v3: per-car stereo cycle banks (32 kHz, 16 bit, built by the existing physical model with per-tailpipe panning and more flow noise) played by the same cycle-synchronous algorithm in a worker thread, plus dynamics (load attack/release, slow modulation, saturation), clips (crackle, shift, tip-in, thumps, blow-off with flutter) and natively mixed loops (turbo tones + hiss, driveline whine); (2) a road layer the game does not have today: own tyres left/right per surface and weather, three-band stereo wind, rumble strip, shoulder, joints, pass-by whooshes; (3) world: environment acoustics by zone, ambience beds, layered collisions and a continuous guardrail scrape, more traffic voices, horns, country siren styles; (4) a loudness plan with scripted ducking and the existing master limiter; (5) music: remastered title theme (same composition), five in-race tracks of about 3:20 each with count-in / loop body / bar-synced ending via AudioStreamInteractive, one calm interlude loop for the screens between stages, tuned UI sounds and result stingers; option "Musik im Rennen" (default on in Modern). Everything is synthesised offline with numpy tools and checked by an automatic QC (loudness, true peak, loop seams, determinism, size).

Deviations from the lead's wording, with evidence: (a) do not switch to 48 kHz – keep the project mix rate at 44.1 kHz and produce Modern music/loops at 44.1 kHz, engine banks at 32 kHz: the mix rate cannot differ per mode at runtime, changing it would route Arcade's title theme through a resampler and break an Arcade test that counts 44.1-kHz frames, and the engine has no content worth it (bank bands above 12.7 kHz are 38 dB or more below the maximum); (b) "Arcade exactly as it is" holds for code paths and assets, but cannot be proven by comparing whole-game recordings because today's engine picks its cycle variants unseeded – prove it with unchanged files plus seeded golden tests instead.

Size: about +47 MB in each archive for the full plan (lean: +39 MB with four tracks at Vorbis q4), on top of today's 15 MB audio that stays for Arcade.

Send the MP3/MP4 previews to the user before the build phase starts: the two A/B pairs (engine old/new, title old/remaster) and the race-mix sketch are the only way to get ears on the direction, and the user's reaction should steer brightness of the road layers, music level under the engine and the musical style.
decisions: Profile = separate implementation, Arcade untouched: AudioManager methods start with a delegation to ModernAudio when profile is modern; engine_audio.gd, engine_bank.gd, engine_gearbox.gd, room_audio.gd, sfx_synth.gd, traffic_audio.gd, assets/audio/{engines,traffic,music} and tools/audio/{engine,traffic,music}_synth.py stay byte-identical. Reason: lowest risk for 'Arcade keeps today's sound exactly'; the Arcade unit tests keep passing unchanged. Modern buses get their own names (prefix M, all into MMaster -> Master) so the Arcade buses and their effect parameters are never touched; only the Master limiter is shared (same ceiling -0.8 dB).

Keep 44.1 kHz as project mix rate; Modern music/ambience/one-shots at 44.1 kHz, engine banks at 32 kHz stereo 16 bit. Evidence: mix rate is fixed at driver start (no per-mode switch); tests/unit/ui/test_audio_synth.gd counts 44100-Hz frames of the Arcade title theme; measured bank spectrum is -38 dB and lower above 12.7 kHz; 32 kHz stereo 16 bit is about 2.2 MB per car (today 1.8–2.3 MB mono float) and costs 2x instead of 3x of today's mixer. All tools get a --rate parameter so a later switch is only a re-render.

Engine v3 keeps the cycle-synchronous algorithm and the physical synthesis, and adds stereo inside the bank instead of separate intake/exhaust runtime layers. Reason: from the chase camera the exhaust dominates; baked stereo needs 4 voices x 2 channels, separate layers would need 8 voices for little gain. Stereo is physical and mono compatible: one listener point, constant-power pan per tailpipe (V8 and boxer banks leave left/right with different pulse trains), independent flow-noise per channel; measured L/R correlation of the new GT bank 0.89 at 2500/min, 0.58 at 5200/min, 0.46 on overrun.

Mixer in a worker thread with a synchronous fallback. Evidence: 1.0–1.15 ms per 1/60 s for stereo 48 kHz (about 0.7 ms at 32 kHz, inferred) is too much on a Deck main thread that is already at 9–13 ms in busy scenes (inferred x1.5); thread test: 0 underruns with six 400-ms hitches vs 535 on the main thread, same CPU (about 6 % of one core), no engine errors. Tests and Movie Maker use the synchronous mode (deterministic); the thread must keep EngineAudio.pump()'s adaptive queue (the Dummy driver pulled blocks of up to about 90 ms in the test).

Turbo, driveline, tyres and wind are loops mixed natively by Godot (pitch_scale and volume per frame), not GDScript samples. Reason: zero per-sample script cost; replaces the pure sine whistle (measured +10 dB tonal spike at 4.9 kHz) by two slightly detuned narrow-band tones with flow hiss per charger.

Own-car road layer is mandatory for Modern: tyres per side and surface (dry, wet hiss, snow, concrete joints, rumble strip, gravel shoulder, grass), three-band stereo wind with gusts, joints with front/rear axle delay from the speed, pass-by whooshes of roadside objects and bridges. Evidence: it is what fills the spectrum at speed (29 of 29 bands, >5 kHz share at 130 km/h -30 -> -17 dB) and gives stereo life; engine-only changes do not fix the cruise drone.

No interior-resonance layer (there is only the chase camera); body weight comes from the bank's low end and the road/wind low band (share below 60 Hz at 266 km/h -17.6 -> -12.8 dB in the demo). Per-car character through the profile data: Kompakt narrow with loud whistle, flutter blow-off and DSG blat; Kombi diesel knock centred, strong turbo, no crackle; Limousine silky and narrow; Sportwagen widest mid-range (two banks), optional induction-howl loop, sharp cracks, no turbo; Gran Turismo wide burble, biturbo left/right, bangs with distant echo.

Modern one-shots are pre-rendered files (numpy tools, stereo, variants via AudioStreamRandomizer/Polyphonic), not SfxSynth at start-up. Reason: quality (44.1 kHz stereo, layered impacts by impulse and partner), no 233-ms synthesis at start, measurable loudness per file in a manifest; SfxSynth stays for Arcade only.

Ducking is scripted (per-frame bus volume from the car-bus level with attack 50 ms, release 450 ms), the AudioEffectCompressor sidechain only as an option. Evidence: sidechain works but a test tone dropped from -15 to -56.5 dB at threshold -30 dB, ratio 4 – far stronger than nominal and hard to predict; scripted ducking is deterministic and unit-testable.

Loudness plan for Modern at default sliders: full throttle -16 LUFS short-term (today -13), cruise about -21, idle about -24; in-race music 8 dB under the car (about -24), about -19 when the car idles; menu music -20 (today -28.7); masters of all music at -14 LUFS, true peak <= -1 dBTP after Vorbis; master limiter as today plus a slow glue compressor on MMaster. Reason: today's 15-dB jump between menu and race; the race-mix sketch shows these relations (car -16.1, music -24.0, sum -15.5 LUFS, true peak -3.75 dBTP).

Races get music in Modern, default on, option 'Musik im Rennen' (Arcade unchanged, no race music). Reasons: genre and brand (OutRun-style title theme), 30–60 min races need it against monotony; safeguards: 8 dB under the car plus ducking, a static mid dip (about -3 dB around 500 Hz) in the music bus while racing, siren and impacts bypass the ducking and the music drops 3 dB while the siren runs. Attract mode stays as today (title theme continues, no race music).

Soundtrack size and form: remastered title theme (3:22, same notes, own file for Modern) + 5 in-race tracks of about 3:20 with different tempo/key/mood (fast lane 132 bpm D minor, night stage about 112 bpm, pass road about 122 bpm, chase about 140 bpm, sunset about 106 bpm), picked by a shuffled queue weighted by hour and weather + one 1:20 interlude loop for result/route screens during a race (today the menu shell restarts the title intro after every stage – read from game_flow.gd, not recorded). Each track = count-in clip (lands on 'Go') -> looping body -> ending at the next bar line; verified: AudioStreamInteractive advanced gaplessly at 2.0 s and switched at the next bar (4.14 s measured, 4.09 s expected plus a 125-ms crossfade). A track that ends mid-stage crossfades into the next body.

Remaster = same arrangement, new production chain, with the low end balanced by band energy instead of LUFS. Evidence from the spike: levelling the 47-Hz kick layer by K-weighted loudness put the sub band 12 dB too hot (-4.3 dB share) until it was set by band energy (-9.5 dB); the chord check must ignore everything below 130 Hz when kick layers are strong (it reported C sharp instead of D before).

Formats: music Ogg Vorbis q5 (1.12 MB/min measured; q4 0.91), ambience beds Vorbis q3–q4, noise loops Vorbis or QOA-compressed WAV, tonal loops and short one-shots 16-bit PCM WAV, engine banks raw interleaved int16 next to the JSON (decode of 1.62 M samples in GDScript measured 46 ms; gzip saves only 6 %). A manifest JSON lists every Modern asset with measured LUFS, peak, loop points and bpm for the tests.

Profile follows the graphics mode (Settings), with a config override audio.profile = auto|arcade|modern for tests. Reason: the task asks for one switch; the override makes Modern sound testable before the 3D renderer exists and Arcade sound testable with it.
plan: Step 0 – contract (owner: lead with package A, before anything else): fix the API additions and names. AudioManager.set_profile(id) / profile(); set_vehicle_state(dict) per frame from the race session {speed, throttle, brake, steer, understeer, lat_g, surface_l, surface_r (asphalt|concrete|cobble|rumble|shoulder|grass), wet, snow, off_road, rail_contact (-1/0/+1), slipstream}; set_environment(env) gets optional keys zone (open|forest|city|cutting|valley), walls, bridge, tunnel_len_m next to the existing tunnel; event(name, args) for joint, pass_object {side, dist_m, size}, collision {impulse, kind, side}, thunder {delay_s}, stage_start {countdown_s}, stage_finish {record, won}, busted, out_of_fuel. All existing calls keep their signatures; Arcade ignores the new ones. Bus names (MMaster, MMusic, MUI, MSfx, MCar, MEngine, MEngineFx, MRoad, MWind, MImpact, MWorld, MTrafficV0..7, MSiren, MAmb, MEnv), asset layout assets/audio/modern/{engines,vehicle,traffic,sfx,ambience,ui,music}/ with manifest.json, config block audio.modern.* and audio.profile.

Package A – core and mix (one agent; files: scripts/audio/audio_manager.gd delegation lines only, new scripts/audio/modern/modern_audio.gd, modern_buses.gd, sfx_bank.gd, scripts/core/settings.gd and scripts/ui/screens/options_screen.gd for 'Musik im Rennen', config/game_config.json audio.modern, docs/audio-modern.md): ModernAudio skeleton that owns all Modern parts and is created/freed by set_profile; bus graph with MEnv as dry + reflections + reverb pass-through (Godot buses have one send); loudness plan, scripted ducking, snapshots (pause low-pass, impact dip, siren dip, result); manifest loader; golden tests that Arcade output of the seeded mixer and the Arcade bus parameters are identical with Modern code present; stubs so packages B–D can plug in independently.

Package B – engine (one agent; files: tools/audio/modern/engine_synth3.py importing tools/audio/engine_synth.py unchanged, scripts/audio/modern/engine_bank2.gd, engine_audio3.gd, engine_mix_thread.gd, vehicle_layers.gd, assets/audio/modern/engines/*, docs/motorsound.md section Modern, tests/unit/audio_modern/test_engine3*.gd): bank format ce-engine-bank-2 (32 kHz, 2 channels, int16, clips crackle x12, shift, start, tipin, thump, blowoff x3, showroom rev clip); stereo mixer = today's algorithm with shared phase/index math for both channels, per-cycle gain jitter, load attack 22 ms / release 60 ms, slow modulators, saturation; thread with mutex-protected control block, adaptive queue as EngineAudio.pump(), synchronous mode for tests/Movie Maker/--audio-sync; turbo and driveline loops; all five cars with their character table; reference prototypes: scratch src/bank3.py, engine3.py, render_new.py. result.recommendation:
Go with the lead's hypothesis (second real-3D renderer in the same build, shared simulation, Arcade untouched), with these product rules:

1. Two independent switches: "Grafik: Arcade / Modern" (Options, page GRAFIK) and "Klang: Arcade / Modern" (page ALLGEMEIN, plus "Musik im Rennen" for Modern). A one-time chooser at the first start of v0.8.0 sets both for new AND existing players; the recommended card is preselected (Modern unless the adapter is a software rasteriser). Menus follow at once, a race takes the mode at its next start; never swap the renderer inside a timed stage.
2. Fallback in three layers: render self-test before the first Modern scene, crash-guard marker file, and a slowness watchdog (automatic preset step-down during the countdown, an offer on the result screen). "--graphics=arcade" on the command line always wins and is the documented rescue switch. A graphics fallback never touches the sound profile.
3. "Das ganze Spiel" for v0.8.0: complete race view for all stages, 3D showroom, loading screen with pre-warm, attract demos in the current mode, Modern fills 16:10 on the Deck, sound profile and music, a built-in "Leistungstest". Title picture, fonts, icons, stage/result/ferry screens and the HUD layout stay as they are; a living 3D title, 3D menu backdrop refinements, HUD skin, pause-menu switching and dynamic resolution may follow in 0.8.x.
4. Testing: enforce "Arcade is pixel-identical" with MD5 goldens generated from tag v0.7.0 (proven to work); keep tools/run_tests.sh a single headless pass (simulation suites run once, plus about 45 s of new headless Modern checks) and put everything that needs OpenGL into a separate tools/run_render_checks.sh that uses fast-forward screenshots. Because nobody can see or time the renderer on a real GPU here, make user review gates (A/B clips, an alpha build, the Leistungstest result from the user's PC and Deck) part of every milestone.
5. Release: bake the 3D models into committed, deterministic mesh resources instead of letting Godot import .glb at build time (otherwise the archives stop being reproducible); add a size report and a size gate to tools/build_release.sh (warn above 300 MB, fail above 330 MB against the 350 MB limit).

AUTOMATIC FALLBACK, three layers. (a) Render self-test before the first Modern scene of a run: a 96×96 SubViewport with a lit sphere and a custom-shader quad, read back and checked; measured 140–156 ms the first time and 46–55 ms afterwards on llvmpipe, passes on OpenGL 4.5 core and OpenGL ES 3.2, reports 'shader' for a deliberately broken shader, is skipped headless. Failure → the stage starts in Arcade with 'Der Modus „Modern“ lässt sich mit dieser Grafik nicht starten. Das Spiel läuft im Modus „Arcade“ weiter.' (b) Crash guard: a marker file user://modern_start.lock is written before the first Modern scene and removed after it has drawn for a while; found at the next start → this run is Arcade and the title asks 'Bei Arcade bleiben' / 'Modern noch einmal versuchen'. (c) Too slow: during the 3 s countdown step the preset down once if clearly below 30 fps (HUD: 'Grafikqualität gesenkt: Niedrig'); after the stage a watchdog (median / p95 frame time) offers 'Qualität senken' or, on the lowest preset, 'Zu Arcade wechseln'. --graphics=arcade on the command line beats choice, marker and everything else (rescue switch for docs/windows.md); a config key graphics.force_mode next to the executable does the same.

Preset values live as data in config graphics.* (tunable next to the executable like every other number). ARCADE PIXEL IDENTITY IS TESTABLE EXACTLY: with --fixed-fps 60 and a seed, Arcade race screenshots are byte-identical run to run, and all 14 frames of the seven attract scenes (bridge, tunnel, city at dusk, snow, night rain, rush hour, lagoon, dawn) have the same MD5 in unmodified v0.7.0 and in the spike build started with --graphics=arcade. So the golden set is a list of hashes generated from tag v0.7.0 on the test machine (regenerated from the tag after a Mesa or Godot change); no reference pictures in the repo. Policy: Modern code lives in new files, Arcade renderer files are not edited.

FAST-FORWARD SCREENSHOTS: switching RenderingServer.render_loop_enabled off until 0.1 s before each shot gives the same hashes and cuts the 14 frames from 385 s to 96 s (one scene 21.1 → 7.4 s). Essential for Modern, where the sibling probe measured 150–170 ms per frame for a heavy 3D scene on llvmpipe.

GOLDEN TOLERANCE ON LLVMPIPE: 3D output is deterministic too (0 differing pixels in the showroom area between two runs; Windows export under Wine identical to Linux; OpenGL ES vs. desktop GL max difference 1 level on 475 pixels, PSNR 85.7 dB). Tiers: same driver → exact hash; other driver or GLES → max channel difference ≤ 2 and PSNR ≥ 60 dB; anything else → 'changed', a contact sheet (reference | new | difference) is written and a human decides. Modern goldens are change detectors during development, Arcade goldens are a hard gate. Wall-clock animations break determinism (the pulsing arrows of the vehicle screen use Time.get_ticks_msec(): about 950 differing pixels) – test runs need a frame-based clock and fixed particle seeds.

WHAT HEADLESS CAN TEST (dummy renderer): ArrayMesh surfaces, vertex read-back and AABB work, a glTF scene instantiates with all 49,984 triangles readable, Camera3D.unproject_position / is_position_in_frustum / get_frustum work. Not available headless: MultiMesh instance read-back (returns zero) and all render counters (0). Consequence: road and terrain mesh builders, chunk streaming, instance lists (kept as plain data by the renderer), LOD and light selection and all camera parity checks go into the normal headless run; draw-call and triangle budgets need Xvfb.

PARITY WITH THE ARCADE PROJECTION: the Arcade camera looks horizontally with the horizon at 45 % of the height – a shifted frustum. A Camera3D with PROJECTION_FRUSTUM and frustum_offset reproduces RoadProjection exactly (max error 0.000 px over 288 points up to 900 m). An ordinary perspective camera pitched 2.9° down is up to 10 px off on screen and shows 38 % instead of 33 % of a car at the depth where the one-third collision rule switches. Decisions: the simulation keeps RoadProjection for the one-third rule in both modes; assertions are (P1) flat straight road ≤ 1 px, (P2) fairness invariants on sampled simulation states of six stage types – every vehicle and gameplay sign visible in Arcade is inside the Modern frustum, not hidden earlier by terrain and not fogged earlier, (P3) a small Xvfb sample with flat 'ID colours' per vehicle comparing visible pixel counts.

RUN_TESTS.SH STAYS ONE PASS. Today it takes 434 s here; about 79 % is simulation (attract scenes 119 s, escapes 84 s, session 41 s, attract 30 s and the simulation-heavy part of the 145 s unit tests) and is independent of the renderer, so it runs once. A new scenario proves that independence by running one session with each renderer class headless and comparing the result and a per-second hash of the traffic. Estimated additions: +35–50 s (inferred, the Modern renderer does not exist yet). Everything needing OpenGL goes into tools/run_render_checks.sh [arcade|modern|all]; estimated 10–12 min in total (Arcade goldens measured: 96 s for 14 frames; Modern estimated 15–25 s per scene).

WINDOWS AND ANGLE: Wine checks of Modern can be exact comparisons with the Linux export (measured identical for the showroom; wine run 21 s). ANGLE cannot be shown under Wine (known: black picture), so the OpenGL ES path on Linux (--rendering-driver opengl3_es) is the proxy for 'the Modern shaders compile as GLSL ES 3.00' and must be part of the render checks; a real Windows PC with --rendering-driver opengl3_angle stays a user check.

EXPORT FILTERS NEED NO CHANGE: with export_filter all_resources the imported scene of a .glb and .gdshader files are packed, the source .glb is not, tests/* stays out (checked in an exported spike build; export takes 5.6 s for Linux and 6.3 s for Windows once imported).

DO NOT IMPORT .GLB AT BUILD TIME – BAKE. Godot 4.7 gives every node of an imported scene a random unique_id, so two imports of the same .glb differ (7 ids for a 7-node car; .godot/ is not committed, so every clean release build would differ) and the documented byte-reproducible archives would end with v0.8.0. Fix that works: a bake script loads the .glb with GLTFDocument and saves node-free mesh resources (.res) with fixed resource_scene_unique_id on the mesh and its materials – byte-identical across runs (without fixed ids the saver writes random 5-character ids). The baked files are committed like the sprite PNGs; .glb stays an intermediate outside the export. .gitattributes must mark *.res, *.scn, *.glb as binary.

SIZE BUDGET (compressed, Windows zip, the larger archive; today 126.9 MB): engine template 38, Arcade sprites 71 and Arcade audio 14.7 unchanged, UI/fonts/scripts/data ≤ 5, Modern meshes ≤ 45, Modern textures ≤ 60, Modern sounds ≤ 15, music ≤ 25 → 274 MB, 76 MB reserve to 350 MB. tools/build_release.sh prints the per-category table and warns above 300 MB, fails above 330 MB. Mesh data is already compressed by Godot (deflate ratio 0.99), so it counts fully: about 27 bytes per triangle with LODs and shadow meshes (importer), 11 bytes per triangle for LOD 0 alone. Deliverables remain the two archives only: the bare .exe is already 413.6 MiB (above the 400 MiB delivery limit) and the Linux binary 379.5 MiB; since v0.6.0 the releases contain only archives.

risks: Deck performance cannot be verified here. No GPU; the GDScript main thread already needs 6–9 ms in busy Arcade scenes on a core about 1.5× faster than the Deck's, and driver cost per draw call on radeonsi is unknown. Mitigation: script-time and draw-call budgets as proxies, Leistungstest plus user gate at M1 before breadth work, presets, automatic step-down.

Look cannot be judged by a human here. Only screenshots reviewed by the agent and the user's eyes at the gates; a style the user dislikes found late would waste the asset breadth (119 environment models, 57 vehicle sets).

Asset breadth and backsides. The generators were built for sprites seen from a few angles; in 3D every side shows. The showroom sprite (Cycles) currently beats the real-time sample model, so 'feinere Modelle' has a high bar.
Scope. The must list for v0.8.0 is large (all stages × weather × time of day plus menus plus audio). The cut line to 0.8.x is explicit, but M3 is the bulk of the work.
Arcade regressions through shared code (session, HUD, settings, GameFlow). Mitigation: hash goldens from v0.7.0 as a hard gate and the 'new files only' policy.

Fairness regressions: a 3D camera, real hills and fog can hide or reveal things at other distances than Arcade; the one-third collision rule depends on the Arcade projection. Mitigation: parity and fairness tests P1–P3, simulation keeps RoadProjection.

Reproducible builds break if .glb is imported at build time (random node ids per import, measured). Mitigation: baked deterministic resources; cost: an estimated 30–60 MB more binaries in the repository.
Archive size creep, mainly textures (facades, foliage, terrain), which is not measured yet. Mitigation: budget per category and the gate at 330 MB.
Shader compilation stutter on first use in the Compatibility renderer (13–81 ms measured by the engine probe on llvmpipe). Mitigation: pre-warm in the loading screen, shader cache, countdown.

Windows on old or integrated graphics and ANGLE: 3D shaders are heavier than today's 2D ones and ANGLE cannot be rendered under Wine. Mitigation: OpenGL ES proxy run, self-test, crash guard, rescue switch, a real Windows test by the user.

Test time on llvmpipe (150–170 ms per heavy 3D frame). Mitigation: fast-forward screenshots, render checks outside run_tests.sh. The Modern timings in this study (15–25 s per scene, +35–50 s headless) are estimates.

Determinism of goldens: wall-clock animations and unseeded particles change pictures between runs (found in the vehicle screen). Needs a frame-based test clock and fixed seeds; particle layers are better checked by assertions than by goldens.
Memory with two asset sets in one build (Arcade texture memory in a race is 247–259 MB today). Each mode must load only its own assets.
The chooser changes every non-headless start without a settings file; tools and Xvfb tests that start the full game without --graphics would hang on it.
Settings migration details (the fullscreen version comparison) can silently change behaviour for existing players if the constant is simply raised.

result.verdict: The lead hypothesis is sound, with three corrections. A second, real-3D renderer on the Compatibility renderer in the same build is feasible and does not disturb Arcade: the engine probe measured bit-identical Arcade frames before and after a 3D scene in one process, and I confirmed that the simulation is unaffected when a 3D renderer forces the track generation 1,900 m ahead (identical stage result, 27 of 27 keys, on dev_testetappe at night in rain and Saragossa–Pau in snow, also with the renderer study's 3D spike). A true world-space road works for all 128 stage directions as long as the world is streamed by path distance. Corrections: (1) "visible at least as early as in Arcade" cannot hold literally in true 3D (one cannot look through the hill a road winds around); it is replaced by tested criteria: everything Arcade shows within 270 m is in view, beyond that the stopping distance is at most 0.6 of the sight distance, and no crest case falls inside the stopping distance. (2) Models cannot simply be "exported as glTF": Blender's exporter loses the procedural materials and Godot's scene import is not byte-reproducible, so the pipeline is an own GLB writer plus a deterministic bake to mesh resources (verified headless and byte-identical); vehicle decals become geometry and vegetation is rebuilt. (3) The Compatibility renderer dictates the lighting design: one shadow-casting light, shadowed light added in sRGB space, few positional lights, no decals/SSR/TAA, shader compile hitches on first use. The largest visual risk the renderer study left open, terrain and horizon not closing in bends, has a remedy that I verified in the spike at four positions including the two worst. Still unverifiable here: GPU frame times on a Steam Deck, ANGLE/Direct3D on Windows, and how the new sound and music actually sound; the plan has three user review gates for exactly these.
conflicts: Chunk size and lights. The engine probe wanted road chunks of 25 m or less and a budget of 24-32 real lamps with distance fade, because a mesh loses lights beyond 8 omni + 8 spot. The renderer study planned 96 m chunks with a pool of six lights and lamp pools computed in the road shader. Resolution: at most 8 omni and 2 spot lights exist at any time, all unshadowed, so the per-object limit can never be reached; chunks stay 96 m, no engine limit is raised, everything else is emissive geometry plus analytical light pools in the road and terrain shaders.

Shadows as a quality option. The engine probe showed that lit brightness depends on the shadow flag (shadowed light is added in sRGB space) and warned against toggling shadows; renderer and product studies both planned 'Schatten: Aus'. Resolution: the sun always keeps shadow_enabled; 'Aus' switches the casters off. Verified: ambient 37 + sun 84 gives 91 without the flag and 120 with it; with the flag and no casters it is also 120 at 3 instead of 15 draw calls, and the value is the same for orthogonal, 2-split and 4-split shadows; sun energy 0 equals ambient only (tunnels).

Glow. The engine probe wanted glow permanently on so the post path never changes the look; the renderer and product studies wanted presets without glow. Resolution: the post path is pinned by Environment.adjustment_enabled in every preset (also selects the post path; within 1 level in my probe), glow becomes a normal preset option.

Sky. The engine probe recommended an own sky shader and forbade BG_COLOR; the renderer study reuses the 2D RaceBackdrop through BG_CANVAS, which gives no sky reflections. Resolution: canvas background for everything visible plus a small Sky resource used only as reflection source. Verified that sky reflections and sky ambient work with a canvas background, also with glow, 3D scale 0.75, MSAA 2x and depth fog.

Surfaces per vehicle. The asset study planned up to 10 role surfaces per car (one per lamp role); the engine probe wants 4-6 surfaces plus wheels and treats draw calls as the main-thread budget. Resolution: one vertex format for all untextured geometry with paint codes in the colour alpha and lamp channels in the second UV set; a traffic car is 2 surfaces + 4 wheels near and 1 surface far. Verified end to end through a compressed mesh resource with per-instance uniforms, a runtime global uniform and a dither fade.

glb import against reproducible archives. The asset study wanted committed .glb files imported by Godot at build time; the product study found that this import is not byte-reproducible (random node ids). Resolution: .glb is only an intermediate; a headless bake writes node-free mesh resources with fixed ids that are committed. Verified: the bake runs headless and is byte-identical across two headless runs and an Xvfb/OpenGL run.

LOD. The engine probe wants to rely on Godot's automatic mesh LOD; the asset study showed that decimating patch-built cars breaks the glazing. Automatic LOD is itself a decimation. Resolution: vehicles get explicit LODs from generator detail levels with hard swap distances; automatic LOD is generated only for models without decal patches (buildings, landmarks, props).

Far LOD and stand-ins. The renderer study wanted the existing sprites as far LOD of every prop (zero extra bytes); the asset study showed the sprite tree models are not acceptable next to new card trees. Resolution: far LOD of a modelled set is an impostor baked from the new model; an Arcade sprite billboard is only the stand-in for a set that has no model yet. Consequence: every stage is drivable in Modern from wave 1 on, no per-stage gating.

One switch or two. The audio study couples the sound profile to the graphics mode; the product study wants two independent switches so a graphics fallback never changes the sound. Resolution: sound_profile = auto | arcade | modern, where auto follows the chosen (not the effective) graphics mode.

Audio hooks from the renderer. The audio study expected pass-by events from the 3D prop placement; that contradicts the rule that every picture/sound combination must work. Resolution: all audio input comes from the session state and from Track segments through a pure AudioFeed.

Vertical slice hides the main visual risk. The product study wanted the slice on Kiel-Hamburg km 0-20 only, which is flat. Resolution: the slice is Kiel-Hamburg complete, but its acceptance includes a terrain gate at four mountain positions (Kassel-Wuerzburg km 46.5 and 61.9, Saragossa-Pau km 172.8 and 198.8).

Terrain closure. The renderer study left a visible void on the outside of climbing bends. I tested a remedy in the spike (about 30 changed lines): the outer terrain ring ends on a 'valley floor' (lowest road within 900 m of path minus 4.5 m), a far-ground plane follows the camera just above it, and the backdrop stands on the true horizon row. The void is gone at the four tested positions; before/after pictures are in the evidence folder.

Frame budgets do not add up between studies. Engine probe: 1,200-1,500 draw calls for the Deck; renderer study: 350 draw calls and 300k triangles; the asset LOD budgets alone give about 200k vehicle triangles. Resolution: one table per preset (Deck: 650 draw calls and 450k primitives including shadow passes, 1.5 ms GDScript for render()), explicitly marked as inferred targets until the user's benchmark result exists.

Near plane. Renderer study 0.3-0.5 m, asset study at least 1.5 m because decal patches z-fight. Resolution: 1.0 m, decal patches at least 1.5 mm above the body and only in the nearest LOD (up to 80 m). The depth-step formula d^2/(near*2^24) reproduces both observations of the asset study.

Shader stutter was understated in the product study (13-81 ms) against the engine probe's measurement (0.5-1.9 s per new shader variant with cold caches). Resolution: warm-up behind the loading overlay is mandatory and has its own cold-cache test.

Mirrored props. The asset study planned pre-mirrored meshes because a mirrored instance inside a MultiMesh renders inside-out. Verified alternative: a MultiMeshInstance3D whose node is mirrored renders identically lit, correctly culled instances, so no second mesh is needed.

16:10. The product study wants Modern to fill the Steam Deck screen, the renderer study left it open. Verified: the frustum camera reproduces the Arcade projection with 0.000 px error at 1280x720, 1280x800 and 1680x720 with a constant focal length, and in the spike at 1280x800 the unchanged HUD code lays itself out to the corners.

Default mode. The product prototype picks Modern by adapter when nothing is stored; that would change every existing tool and test run on a real GPU. Resolution: without a stored choice the game is Arcade; interactive players get a one-time chooser that appears only when the game starts without any user argument and not headless.

Gaps none of the studies covered, now in the contract: in Modern the session must not preload the 281 MB of vehicle sprite sheets; the new raw engine bank files need a new entry in the export include filter; vehicles inside tunnels beyond the shadow distance would be sunlit (per-instance sun mask); shader global uniforms would break branches that lack their declaration (added at runtime instead); screenshot times must count from 'renderer prepared' so A/B pictures show equal simulation states; pause must freeze the picture.

Names diverged across the studies (scripts/race3d against scripts/race/modern, assets/models against assets/models3d, --gfx against --graphics, ModelDB as autoload, three different renderer class names). The contract fixes one set of paths, class names, flags and setting keys.

Sample rate and size. The brief mentioned 48 kHz; the audio study's evidence (mix rate fixed at start, an Arcade test counting 44.1 kHz frames, confirmed in the test file) keeps 44.1 kHz. The product study's sound budget (15 MB) was below the audio plan (23 MB); the contract uses 23 + 25 MB. Sum for the larger archive: 127 MB today + at most 100 MB models and textures + at most 48 MB audio = at most 277 MB against the 350 MB limit.
decision_record: Engine: GL Compatibility for both modes, switched without restart. No project-wide render state changes; MSAA 3D, 3D scale and shadow settings are set on entering Modern and restored on leaving. Rendering stays on the main thread, so draw calls are a CPU budget.

Arcade is frozen: the Arcade renderer files, Track, all gameplay and data scripts, Arcade audio classes, sprites and Arcade audio assets are not edited at all; sprites are not re-rendered. Identity is a hard gate: a hash list of 20 frames generated from tag v0.7.0 must stay identical after every package.

World: true world-space 3D from the same Track (heading integrated per 3 m segment), chunks of 32 segments (96 m) streamed by path distance, floating origin, no world-space caches. Builders take every position from the path/chunk context so the sheared Arcade-parity mapping remains a fallback.

Camera: Camera3D frustum that equals the Arcade projection exactly (focal 711 logical px at any aspect, horizon at 45 % of the height, near 1.0 m, far 2,600 m) plus a look-into-the-curve yaw of 0.6 x the bearing 100 m ahead. Modern fills the window (stretch aspect expand); Arcade keeps its bars.

Fairness is defined by seven tested criteria: frustum parity within 270 m; beyond that stopping distance at most 0.6 of the sight distance; no crest case inside the stopping distance; depth fog never stronger than Arcade's; vehicles and signs fade by path distance with Arcade's law; lamps keep Arcade's minimum screen size; terrain never rises above road level inside the sight corridor. Records and leaderboards are shared, with a hidden mode field.

Terrain: ruled ribbon owned by each chunk with rings up to 480 m (1,000 m on the highest detail level), clamped on the inside of bends; the outer edge ends on the valley floor, a far-ground plane follows the camera, the backdrop stands on the true horizon.

Light: exactly one shadow-casting light (sun or moon) whose shadow flag is always on; at most 8 omni and 2 spot lights, unshadowed; all other lamps are emissive with glow plus analytical light pools in the road and terrain shaders. The post path is pinned on; tonemapper linear; background is the 2D backdrop on a canvas layer with a small sky resource for reflections only. Unavailable engine features (decals, SSR, TAA/FXAA, volumetric fog, alpha hash, particle trails) are not used.
Shader warm-up behind the loading overlay is mandatory; fog mode, shadow split mode and filter quality are constant for a whole stage.

Assets: the existing Blender generators are the source of every model. Pipeline: generators, own GLB writer, intermediate .glb in a git-ignored cache, headless Godot bake to node-free mesh resources without embedded materials, committed with a generated manifest. Changes inside the sprite generators are additive hooks guarded by a geometry regression fixture.

Materials: five material classes (vertex-PBR, glass, baked atlas, baked cut-out, leaves). All untextured geometry uses one vertex format (albedo in the vertex colour, paint code in its alpha, roughness/metallic in UV, lamp channel and weight in UV2); paint colour, lamp states, fade and a sun mask are per-instance shader parameters.

LODs come from generator detail levels for vehicles (never from decimating finished cars); automatic mesh LOD only for models without decal patches. Vegetation is rebuilt as card foliage with impostors. Textures are S3TC with fixed size tiers. Mirrored props use a mirrored MultiMesh node. Every sprite set resolves to a model or an explicit sprite/box stand-in.

Audio: the Modern sound is a second implementation behind the unchanged AudioManager API with its own buses; Arcade audio stays byte-identical. Mix rate stays 44.1 kHz. Engine v3 uses stereo cycle banks (32 kHz, 16 bit) mixed in a worker thread with a synchronous fallback; tyres, wind, turbo and driveline are natively mixed loops. All audio input comes from the simulation and Track.

Loudness and music: full throttle -16 LUFS short-term, in-race music 8 dB below the car with scripted ducking, masters at -14 LUFS and at most -1 dBTP. Music must-haves: remastered title theme, three race tracks with count-in, loop body and bar-synced ending, one interlude loop, stingers; tracks 4-5 only if time allows.

Settings (file version 3): graphics_mode, sound_profile (auto follows the chosen graphics mode), a quality preset plus five quality values, race_music. Mode resolution: command line, then config force, then crash guard, then stored choice, else Arcade. A one-time chooser at the first interactive start for new and existing players.
A mode change applies in the menus at once and in a race from the next stage start; the renderer is never swapped inside a timed stage.

Fallback in three layers: render self-test before the first Modern scene, a crash-guard marker file, and a slowness watchdog (one automatic preset step-down during the countdown, an offer on the result screen). A failed self-test or a broken model manifest starts the stage in Arcade with a message; --graphics=arcade is the rescue switch.

Quality options expose only what the renderer honours: preset, shadows, details, 3D resolution scale, MSAA, effects. Quality settings never thin out or dim anything the player must react to. Adapter tier is recognised by name; the chooser recommends Modern for normal GPUs and the Deck, Arcade for software and old integrated graphics.

Scope of 'the whole game' in v0.8.0: complete race view for every stage, weather and time of day; 3D showroom per car only where the real-time model is at least as good as its Cycles sprite; loading overlay with warm-up; attract demos in the current mode; unchanged HUD code; a built-in performance test; Modern sound and music. Title picture, map, stage, result, leaderboard and ferry screens stay unchanged.

Tests: tools/run_tests.sh stays one headless pass (Modern adds about one minute, including the fairness and world checks); everything that needs OpenGL goes into a separate render-check script with fast-forward screenshots. Arcade goldens are exact hashes; Modern goldens are change detectors; Modern correctness is asserted by render checks. A deterministic test mode (--gfx-sync, --audio-sync) is mandatory.

Budgets: larger archive at most 277 MB planned (warning above 300, build failure above 330, hard limit 350); texture memory in a Modern race at most 260 MB; per-preset draw-call, primitive and script-time budgets (Deck: 650 / 450,000 / 1.5 ms) as inferred targets; asset budgets per category enforced by a validator. Deliverables are the two archives only.

Three user review gates (after the vertical slice, after one whole race in all conditions, at beta) deliver A/B sheets, clips, audio previews and a test build with the performance test, because GPU performance, ANGLE and the sound cannot be judged on this machine.
build_plan: Structure: nine waves with at most four packages in parallel. M0 = wave 0 (scaffolding of the slice). M1 = waves 1-2 (vertical slice: Kiel-Hamburg end to end in Modern with real assets, option switch, screenshots, test build; ends with gate 1). M2 = waves 3-5 (all conditions, special sections, all vehicles, vegetation, first cities; ends with gate 2). M3 = waves 6-7 (all of Europe, effects, the whole game; ends with gate 3). M4 = wave 8 (performance, acceptance, docs, release). Every package is done only when its checks pass, tools/run_tests.sh is green, the Arcade hash check is identical, and no file outside its ownership changed. Shared files have exactly one owner per wave (table in section 5 of the contract).

Wave 0, package KERN (core, session seam, tools). Owns scripts/core/{gfx, gfx_self_test, settings, screenshotter}.gd, scripts/race/{race_renderers, race_session}.gd, a stub scripts/race3d/modern_renderer.gd, export presets, .gitattributes, the graphics config section, tools/{golden, run_render_checks, run_tests}.sh, pck_report.py, the size gate in build_release.sh. Inputs: the product study's prototype diffs. Outputs: settings v3, mode resolution, command-line flags, renderer factory and session flow with loading overlay, fallback and crash guard, audio hook call sites, hash list from tag v0.7.0. Acceptance: settings migration tests including the fullscreen trap; 20 of 20 Arcade hashes identical; identical stage result for both modes on two stages; forced failure falls back to Arcade with the message; both exports build.

Wave 0, package PIPE (asset pipeline core and reference models). Owns tools/blender/ce3d, export_models.py, validate_models.py, the sprite geometry fixture, tools/models (bake, contact sheet), scripts/core/model_db.gd, the four model shaders and material/model factory scripts, assets/models. Inputs: the asset study's prototype exporter and the bake probes. Outputs: full pipeline, manifest with an entry for every sprite set, reference set (one player car with race, showroom and shadow meshes, one traffic sedan with three LODs and four colours, a card-foliage oak with impostor, one baked farmhouse, a streetlight, one landmark). Acceptance: validator green, two bakes byte-identical, day and night contact sheets, sprite geometry unchanged, all 180 non-UI sets resolve.

Wave 0, package AU-A (audio core). Owns the delegation lines in audio_manager.gd, scripts/audio/modern, tools/audio/modern and tools/audio/qc, placeholder assets and manifests, the audio.modern config keys. Outputs: ModernAudio skeleton, bus graph, loudness plan with scripted ducking, AudioFeed, music director stub, quality-control tool. Acceptance: all existing audio tests unchanged and green, Arcade engine mixer output byte-identical in a seeded test, 20 profile switches leave no extra node or bus, a headless race with the Modern profile runs without errors.

Wave 0, package GEO (geometry kernel and fairness checks). Owns scripts/race3d/{road_path, chase_camera, terrain_profile, chunk_context, chunk_builder, chunk_streamer, builder_registry}.gd, their unit tests, tests/sim/modern_sight.gd and modern_path_check.gd. Inputs: the renderer study's path prototype and scan scripts, my valley-floor diffs. Acceptance: arcs match the closed form, camera math within 0.5 px of the Arcade projection at three aspect ratios, the study's numbers reproduced in full mode (minimum clearance 267.6 m, zero frustum cases up to 270 m, worst stopping ratio at most 0.60, zero crest cases), sampled run at most 45 s, deterministic streamer.

Wave 1, package R1 (renderer core). Owns modern_renderer.gd, environment rig, quality, warm-up, road and roadside builders, backdrop/lights/overlay layers, road shader. Outputs: Kiel-Hamburg drivable in Modern with all road paint in the shader, guardrails, sun with shadows, palette-driven fog and ambient, backdrop at any aspect, headlights, HUD over 3D, warm-up, perf statistics, debug snapshot. Acceptance: lane-line pixels within 1 px on a straight, daylight colours within 10 % of Arcade, equal brightness with shadows off, core at most 0.6 ms GDScript per frame, 1280x800 and 1680x720 filled, cold-cache warm-up check, stage result equal to Arcade.

Wave 1, package R2 (terrain, props, far ground). Owns terrain and props builders, far-ground layer, prop library, terrain/billboard shaders. Outputs: ribbon terrain with the valley-floor closure, props as MultiMesh per chunk with mirrored nodes, LOD ranges, sprite stand-ins. Acceptance (terrain gate): at most 0.2 % uncovered pixels below the horizon at six reference positions, A/B sheet of the four mountain positions without void or visible ribbon edge, no overlapping terrain between chunks, prop lists equal the track's props, fairness terrain rule green.

Wave 1, package R3 (vehicles and signs). Owns vehicle and flare layers, sign atlas and sign builder, sign/flare shaders, takes over the vehicle shaders. Outputs: vehicle pool with pose from two path points, wheels, LODs, lamp states, minimum-size flares, path-distance fade, shadow or blob shadow, articulated trucks; all sign textures pre-rendered through the existing SignPainter. Acceptance: footprint equals the collision box within 0.3 m, lamps follow the view flags, indicator and tail-light visibility checks, occlusion checks (0 pixels), no texture created during the drive, every sign kind drawn, at most 40 microseconds per car.

Wave 1, package AS1 (slice vehicles). Owns the car and truck generator files (hooks) and the vehicle exporters. Outputs: two player cars (race, showroom, shadow meshes), three traffic bodies with geometry decals and three LODs, the truck with tractor and trailer parts, all their colour sets. Acceptance: validator, contact sheets, A/B showroom sprite against real-time model, at most 6 draw calls per near traffic car, sprite geometry unchanged.

Wave 2 (ends with gate 1). UI1: options with two pages, chooser, showroom widget, loading overlay progress, benchmark screen, crash-guard question, hidden mode field in leaderboard entries; acceptance: gamepad end-to-end check 10/10, existing pad checks unchanged, chooser condition matrix tested, screens fit 1280x720 and 1280x800. AS1b: environment models of the slice (trees, bushes, farm buildings, wind turbine, road furniture, fuel station parts); acceptance: no sprite stand-in in the first 75 km of Kiel-Hamburg. AU-B: engine v3 for five cars; acceptance: click, balance and mono tests, -16 LUFS at full throttle, zero underruns with main-thread hitches, sample-identical sync mode, A/B previews. QA1: render checks, benchmark runner, A/B sheets and clips for all reference positions, Wine and OpenGL ES smoke runs, test build of both platforms, gate-1 package.

Wave 3. R4: night calibration, light pool, analytical pools, rain and snow particles, wet road, snow, sky reflections; acceptance: tail-light visibility at night, no light through hills or trucks, luminance table per weather and hour, light cap holds. R5: tunnels with portal and mound, bridges with water; acceptance: Gotthard and Somport checks, every bridge of the network builds. R6: fuel station, border, city fixtures, start and finish gantries, radar; acceptance: A/B sheets of every element on the dev stage, fuel-lane geometry equals the track. AS2a: remaining three player cars with interiors, remaining traffic bodies; acceptance: all 26 car sets resolve to models.

Wave 4. AS2b: trucks, buses, 18 police sets with beacons. AS3: nine tree species in two variants, bushes, rocks, cliff; acceptance: silhouettes match the sprites, overdraw report. AU-C1: tyres, wind, joints, impacts and the audio feed; acceptance: click-free loops, worst case at most -0.5 dBTP. AU-D1: music tool chain, title remaster (same notes, checked), race track 1 with gapless count-in, loop and ending; a sketch goes to the user first.

Wave 5 (ends with gate 2). AS4: rural buildings, remaining road furniture, bridge parts, boats. AS5a: city buildings of eight styles (23 sets) with baked atlases. R7: landmarks on the path up to 1,900 m with Arcade's haze law, impostors, LOD tuning; acceptance: A/B sheets of ten city arrivals, landmark where Arcade shows it. QA-mid: the whole race Kiel-Nuernberg in every condition, all render checks, benchmark per preset, test build 2.

Wave 6. AS5b: city buildings of the remaining seven styles (23 sets). AS6: 33 landmarks with atlas or vertex-colour bake and an all-round check. AU-D2: race tracks 2-3, interlude, stingers, UI sounds. AU-C2: environment acoustics, ambience beds, traffic extras, sirens. Acceptance per the studies plus validator, audio quality-control tool and the size report.

Wave 7 (ends with gate 3). R8: canvas sky shader with clouds, wet-road reflections and SSAO for the highest effects level, spray, screen effects; acceptance: effects levels differ only in effects. UI2: performance test final, watchdog offers, attract mode in Modern, final texts and docs for Steam Deck and Windows. AU-E: audio integration and loudness verification on recorded races. QA2: every stage direction 60 s headless in Modern with a leak check, contact sheets of all 22 sceneries and 55 city arrivals, beta build.

Wave 8. PERF: budgets per preset at all benchmark positions, Deck preset tuned against the user's results, warm-up completeness, leaks, memory. QA3: final Arcade hashes, all checks, full fairness scan, Wine and OpenGL ES, size gate, reproducibility of the archives. DOC: German docs, README section, new screenshots. REL: version bump and release build; upload to the draft release only on the lead's explicit instruction.
interfaces: Renderer seam. scripts/race/race_renderers.gd creates RoadRenderer (Arcade, unchanged) or scripts/race3d/modern_renderer.gd (ModernRenderer, Node3D). Both: setup(track, proj, cfg, scenery_db), render(view) every frame, perf_stats(). Modern only, called through has_method: apply_quality(levels) once before prepare(); prepare(ctx) with ctx = {sets, plan, vehicle, weather, hour, sync}; is_prepared(); prepare_progress(); healthy(); fail_reason(); debug_snapshot(); world_to_screen(z, x, h); signal quality_lowered(preset).

Session flow. Mode = setup.gfx or Settings.effective_graphics().mode. In Modern: write the crash-guard marker, create the renderer, set stretch aspect expand, apply quality, prepare behind the loading overlay (no simulation step, no countdown, the screenshot timer does not count until prepared), fall back to the Arcade renderer with the fixed German message when healthy() is false, preload only UI icons through SpriteDB, remove the marker after 2 s of frames. Results carry gfx and gfx_fallback.

View dictionary: unchanged. Added in wave 0 and ignored by Arcade: hour, dt, player.type. No renderer may require a key the session does not send in both modes. Canvas layers: -10 Modern backdrop, 1 Modern screen effects, 2 Modern 2D overlays, 5 HUD (existing), 6 loading overlay.

Settings keys (settings_version 3, each written only once chosen, unknown keys kept): graphics_mode (arcade|modern), sound_profile (auto|arcade|modern), gfx_preset (deck|low|medium|high|custom), gfx_custom {shadows 0-3, details 0-2, scale 50-150, aa 0-2, effects 0-2}, race_music. Settings API: effective_graphics(), is_modern(), quality(), quality_levels(), sound(), adapter_tier(), signals graphics_changed, quality_changed, sound_profile_changed. The fullscreen check compares against the fixed constant 2, not the new version.

Gfx helper (scripts/core/gfx.gd, pure static): classify_adapter, recommended_mode, recommended_preset, resolve_mode(chosen, cli, force, marker), quality, preset_of, sanitized, with_cli, levels, watchdog_verdict; marker file user://modern_start.lock. GfxSelfTest.run(parent) returns {ok, reason, ms}.

Command-line flags after '--': --graphics=arcade|modern (wins over everything), --gfx-preset=, --gfx=key=value list, --gfx-sync (deterministic test mode), --gfx-debug=cover|ids|nolight|chunks|wire|fail, --no-prewarm, --no-watchdog, --sound=arcade|modern, --audio-sync, --shot-fast, --bench= and --bench-out=, --no-chooser. The chooser appears only when no user argument is given.

Config: new top-level section graphics {force_mode, presets, levels, modern {camera, chunk_segments, load_path_m, landmark_path_m, fog, terrain, lights, sky_update_s, prewarm, threaded_build}, watchdog, benchmark, budgets}; audio gets profile and modern. No existing key changes.

race3d coordinates and kernel. World: +X right, +Y up, heading 0 looks along -Z, a positive curve turns right. RoadPath3D: setup, ensure, point, heading, centre_at, heading_at, world(z, x, h), frame_at, rebase, trim, clearance, floor_y. ChaseCamera3D: look_yaw, transform, frustum (focal 711 px), static project. TerrainProfile: ring_offsets, height, corridor_width.

Chunk contract. ChunkContext is a snapshot of 33 rows (segment fields with sprites, row centres, right and forward vectors, road edges, valley floor, terrain ring distances and heights) with local(), frame() and ground(); path and terrain objects are main-thread only. ChunkBuilder: id(), collect(ctx) on the main thread, build(ctx, input) on a worker thread with arrays only, commit(ctx, part, parent) on the main thread, debug(part). Builders and layers are loaded by fixed file names from scripts/race3d/builders and scripts/race3d/layers (registry written once in wave 0), so later packages only add files.

Shader globals with the prefix ce_ (night, wet, snow, time, wind, fog colour and range, sun direction and colour, ambient, tunnel, headlight position, direction and range, far-ground height) are added at runtime by ModernMaterials.ensure_globals(); nothing is declared in project.godot; Modern shaders are loaded with load() after that call, never with preload().

Model pipeline commands: export_models.py (generators to intermediate .glb in tools/blender/_cache3d), tools/models/bake_models.gd (headless Godot to assets/models/<group>/<name>/*.res plus a model.json fragment and textures), export_models.py --manifest-only (merged manifest, regenerated after every merge), validate_models.py, models_contact_sheet.sh.

Model node conventions: LOD nodes lod0, lod1, lod2, optional show (showroom) and shadow; vehicle parts body and wheel_<axle><l|r> with axle 0 in front, pivot at the wheel centre, spin about local X; tractor and trailer groups for articulated vehicles; far LODs are one merged mesh. Model space: nose or far side of a prop points to -Z, vehicle origin on the ground under the centre of the collision box, prop origin at the sprite anchor.

Material classes are the surface names of baked meshes: vpbr, glass, baked, baked_cutout, leaves. The vpbr vertex format: COLOR.rgb albedo (sRGB), COLOR.a paint code (1 fixed, 0 paint, 0.25 paint2, 0.5 paint3), UV = roughness and metallic, UV2.x = lamp channel + 0.5 or -1, UV2.y = lamp weight. Lamp channels: 0 tail, 1 brake, 2 tail+brake, 3 and 4 indicators, 5 head, 6 daytime, 7 reverse, 8 plate, 9 marker, 10 and 11 beacons, 12 night lights of props, 13 always on, 14 flood-lit surface. Per-instance parameters: paint, paint2, paint3, lamp_a, lamp_b, fade, sun.

Model manifest (assets/models/manifest.json, version 1): models {kind, object size equal to the sprite manifest within 2 %, lods with parts (node, mesh path, classes, position, wheel data), shadow mesh, light anchors by role, paint defaults, textures, auto_lod, tags, bytes, hash} and sets (every sprite set id except ui/* maps to a model with paint, a showroom flag, variants, or a fallback 'sprite' or 'box'). ModelDB is a static, lazily loaded class (not an autoload): available, reload, resolve, has_model, object_size, mesh, texture, request, pending, release_all.

Audio API. AudioManager keeps every existing method and adds set_profile(id), profile(), set_race_music(on), set_music_context(ctx), set_track(track, plan), set_vehicle_state(state) every frame, event(name, args); all additions are no-ops in the Arcade profile. State keys: z, x, speed, throttle, brake, steer, understeer, lat_speed, off_road, rail_contact, road_left, road_right, shoulder_m, in_tunnel, weather, hour, crash, finished. Events: stage_start, countdown, go, collision, rail_hit, radar_flash, chase_start, escaped, busted, refuel_start, refuel_done, out_of_fuel, tow, stage_finish.

Audio assets and buses: assets/audio/modern/{engines, vehicle, traffic, sfx, ambience, ui, music}, each folder with its own manifest; engine banks as <car>.json plus <car>.i16 (the extension is added to the export include filter and .gitattributes); buses prefixed M created at runtime; music Ogg Vorbis, everything at 44.1 kHz except the 32 kHz engine banks.

UI contracts: options with the pages ALLGEMEIN and GRAFIK and fixed German labels; chooser 'GRAFIK WAEHLEN'; Showroom3D as a child of CarShowcase with a SubViewport sized in physical pixels; LoadingOverlay.set_progress; fixed German fallback, crash-guard and watchdog messages; performance test with runner class ModernBenchmark and a result written to user://leistungstest.json in a fixed format.

Test and tool contracts: tools/run_tests.sh runs every tests/race3d/check_*.gd and tests/sim/modern_*.gd headless (output lines 'CHECK <name> OK|FEHLER'); tools/run_render_checks.sh runs tests/race3d/render/check_*.gd under Xvfb ('RENDER-CHECK ...'); tools/golden.sh make and check; tests/race3d/bench_modern.gd compares counters with the budgets; named reference positions (S1-S5 slice, T1-T4 terrain, N1, N2, C1, U1, B1, DEV) are used by checks, A/B sheets and gates.

Quality levels: shadows 0-3 (casters none / vehicles and structures / plus buildings and tree proxies / all; atlas 1024-4096; 80-200 m), details 0-2 (vehicle and prop LOD distances, decorative density, outer terrain ring), MSAA off/2x/4x, 3D scale 50-150 %, effects 0-2 (glow, particle counts, spray, wet reflections, SSAO, sky reflections, 2/4/8 pooled lights). Presets: deck {1,1,100,1,1}, low {0,0,75,0,0}, medium {2,1,100,1,1}, high {3,2,100,2,2}.

Budgets as shared numbers: per preset draw calls including shadow passes / primitives / render() GDScript average: deck 650 / 450,000 / 1.5 ms, low 400 / 250,000 / 1.2 ms, medium 900 / 700,000 / 1.5 ms, high 1,500 / 1,500,000 / 2.0 ms; asset triangle budgets (player race mesh 55,000, traffic car 18,000 / 6,000 / 1,200, truck or bus 25,000 / 7,000 / 1,500, tree 2,500 / 900 / impostor, city building 10,000, landmark 25,000); meshes at most 40 MB, textures at most 60 MB in the archive, sounds 23 MB, music 25 MB.
top_risks: GPU performance on the Steam Deck and weak PCs is unmeasured. Everything here ran on a CPU rasteriser; draw calls, triangles and script times are measured, the frame budgets are inferred. Mitigation: benchmark and test build at gate 1 before the breadth work depends on the presets, automatic step-down, Arcade recommended on weak hardware.

Look and feel cannot be judged by a human here: style, the curve camera (the car moves up to about 10 % of the screen width off centre in the tightest bends), night brightness. A style the user dislikes found late would waste the asset breadth. Mitigation: gates with A/B sheets and clips after wave 2 and wave 5.

Terrain in true 3D. The valley-floor closure worked at four spike positions, but tunnels portals, bridges, city arrivals and the inside of tight bends are untested. Mitigation: terrain gate in wave 1 with a coverage check; last resort is the sheared Arcade-parity mapping, for which the builders keep three rules.

Asset breadth and quality bar. The generators were modelled for one sprite view: blank back walls, crude traffic fronts, lamps smeared around corners; vegetation must be rebuilt; the Cycles showroom sprites currently look better than the real-time sample model. This is the largest work item (about 155 models, roughly three hours of bakes on shared cores). Mitigation: per-set stand-ins keep every stage drivable, showroom flag per car, validator budgets.

Windows on ANGLE/Direct3D 11 and old integrated graphics is untested for 3D (Wine cannot run ANGLE). Mitigation: self-test, crash guard, rescue switch, OpenGL ES run on Linux as a proxy, a real Windows check by the user.

Shader compile stutter on first use (0.5-1.9 s per variant with cold caches on this machine). If the warm-up misses a state combination (first lamp in range, first tunnel, rain starting) the player sees a hitch in the race. Mitigation: warm-up generated from the materials and light states the stage really uses, cold-cache test per milestone.

Fairness can regress through art rather than code: terrain relief or vegetation inside bends, darker nights, small lights. Mitigation: the fairness criteria are headless tests and render checks that gate every package; thresholds are not relaxed without the lead.

Arcade regressions through the shared files that must be edited (race session, settings, GameFlow, AudioManager, HUD). Mitigation: exact frame hashes from tag v0.7.0 and a seeded audio comparison as hard gates, new code in new files.

Sound and music have never been heard by anyone; all claims are measurements. The road layers may hiss, the remaster may be too bright, hand-written tracks may be bland; the engine mixer thread is verified only headless on Linux. Mitigation: user previews at the gates, parameters in data, synchronous mixer fallback, minimal music fallback (remaster and interlude only, race music off by default).

Scope and machine load: 36 packages over nine waves on four shared cores, with Blender bakes, software-rendered checks and audio renders competing. Mitigation: explicit cut lines (music tracks 4-5, traffic interiors, 3D title and menu backgrounds, HUD skin moved to later versions), bake-heavy packages never scheduled together with render-heavy QA.

Archive size and memory creep, mainly baked textures (190-230 MB of S3TC in the package, about 50 MB in the archive) and two asset sets in one process. Mitigation: size table and gate at every test build, fixed texture tiers, each mode loads only its own assets.
questions_for_user: Ein Schalter oder zwei? Empfehlung: Die Wahl 'Grafik: Arcade / Modern' stellt Bild und Klang gemeinsam um ('Klang: Wie Grafik'); wer möchte, kann den Klang in den Optionen getrennt auf Arcade oder Modern stellen (z. B. neuer Klang auf schwacher Grafik).
Soll im Modus Modern während des Rennens Musik laufen? Empfehlung: ja, als Vorgabe an ('Musik im Rennen: An', abschaltbar); Arcade bleibt wie bisher ohne Rennmusik.
Erster Start von v0.8.0: Sollen auch bestehende Spieler einmalig den Auswahlbildschirm 'Grafik wählen' sehen? Empfehlung: ja, einmalig für alle; niemand wird stillschweigend umgestellt.

Können Sie Vorabversionen auf einem Steam Deck und einem Windows-PC ausprobieren und das Ergebnis des eingebauten Leistungstests zurückschicken (nach dem ersten spielbaren Abschnitt, nach einem ganzen Rennen, vor dem Release)? Empfehlung: ja; ohne diese Rückmeldung bleibt die Steam-Deck-Voreinstellung vorsichtig, und auf schwacher oder unbekannter Hardware wird Arcade vorgeschlagen.
Bestenlisten: gemeinsam für beide Modi oder getrennt? Empfehlung: gemeinsam, weil Strecke, Verkehr und Fahrphysik identisch sind; der Modus wird unsichtbar mitgespeichert.
Steam Deck (16:10): Soll Modern den ganzen Bildschirm füllen, während Arcade seine Balken behält? Empfehlung: ja.
Bleiben Titelbild, Karte, Etappen- und Ergebnisbildschirme in beiden Modi unverändert (ein lebendiger 3D-Titel könnte später folgen)? Empfehlung: ja.

Umfang zum Release: überarbeitete Titelmelodie plus drei neue Rennmusikstücke (weitere später), Innenräume nur bei den fünf Spielerautos, landesspezifische Sirenen und Kennzeichen später. Ist dieser Zuschnitt in Ordnung? Empfehlung: ja.

Kurvenkamera: In Modern dreht die Sicht leicht in die Kurve (das Auto wandert in den engsten Kurven bis etwa 10 % der Bildbreite aus der Mitte). Soll das die Vorgabe sein? Empfehlung: ja, endgültig entscheiden nach dem Probespielen der ersten Vorabversion.
